Latest Update: Scientists Are Using Your Unhinged Driving Behaviors In Grand Theft Auto To Make Roads Safer

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that as you're preparing to explore all of 212 GB's worth of "Grand Theft Auto VI" and go on the ultimate chaotic crime driving spree in the game's Florida-like state of Leonida, scientists are gearing up for their own run through the new game.
  • It has been revealed that if scientists want to look at how humans react to dangerous situations on the road, what game has better scenarios than GTA?
  • According to recent reports, pavlo Bazilinskyy, a human factors engineer at Eindhoven University of Technology in the Netherlands, told the BBC that a video game with such a massive budget is "miles ahead of the average simulator setup." GTA provides a realistic environment for Bazilinskyy and his fellow researchers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that as you're preparing to explore all of 212 GB's worth of "Grand Theft Auto VI" and go on the ultimate chaotic crime driving spree in the game's Florida-like state of Leonida, scientists are gearing up for their own run through the new game. GTA's years of detailed city streets, paired with drivers' unhinged behaviors behind the wheel have unintentionally created a solid test bed for a variety of scientific studies aimed at making real-life driving and travel safer, according to the BBC.

It has been revealed that if scientists want to look at how humans react to dangerous situations on the road, what game has better scenarios than GTA? The game's detailed city maps and roads also help make the science cheaper.

According to recent reports, pavlo Bazilinskyy, a human factors engineer at Eindhoven University of Technology in the Netherlands, told the BBC that a video game with such a massive budget is "miles ahead of the average simulator setup." GTA provides a realistic environment for Bazilinskyy and his fellow researchers. It's an ideal space for them to use technology like eye-tracking, or more specifically, cyclist behavior as they head towards hazardous situations.

Intel Labs and Darmstadt University in Germany shared a paper in 2016 on how the two used Grand Theft Auto's road scenes and objects to teach AI how to detect both. MIT Technology Review wrote that using the video game's already categorized imagery and streets would help researchers save thousands upon thousands of hours trying to collect and label that street imagery. The game's addition of changes in time and weather, which can both influence the road conditions, helps models experience realities that are difficult and expensive for researchers to recreate digitally.

Institutions like the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology conduct similar research today, using GTA to help train its AI driving software to avoid dangers on the road. In the U.S., at Eastern Michigan University, researchers have used GTA to train an AI's ethical decision-making. EMU's work found that the tests helped reduce fatal accidents by 24%.

In a recent development, there are devices right now in development that could alert cyclists and pedestrians of upcoming hazards on busy roads, acting like a sixth sense for detecting traffic behind them. To test one of these devices, researchers at the Osnabrück University of Applied Sciences in Germany placed participants on a stationary bike with screens showing GTA V in front of and behind them. The devices successfully spotted traffic as it headed towards the cyclists, but without the inherent danger that would be a part of testing the device on a real road.

Science and road safety may be the two furthest things from the average GTA player's mind come Friday, when the sixth installment is available for gameplay. However, scientists and researchers will likely be thrilled to have a newer, even more realistic setting to play with.

The Smallest V10 To Ever Power A Car Was The Size Of Most 4-Cylinders

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • V10 engines are the ultimate metaphors for what gearheads love about performance cars — relics of a bygone era where noise, power and absolute combustion were the go-to recipes of kings.
  • It has been revealed that but aside from the actual cylinder count, what these cars all have in common is big displacements.
  • Industry observers note that for some perspective, many passenger cars these days use 2.0-liter four-cylinder engines, including the Honda Civic hatchback, which is the platonic ideal of economy cars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

V10 engines are the ultimate metaphors for what gearheads love about performance cars — relics of a bygone era where noise, power and absolute combustion were the go-to recipes of kings. The Lexus LFA and Porsche Carrera GT – arguably two of the greatest road-going supercars ever – used them. So too did the Sesto Elemento, which was Lamborghini's answer to the very essence of track-day hoonery. They even featured in the E60-generation BMW M5 – a perhaps ugly but elegant grand tourer that made a mockery of purpose-built, seven-figure unobtanium thanks to an unrestricted 200-mph-plus top speed.

It has been revealed that but aside from the actual cylinder count, what these cars all have in common is big displacements. The LFA's V10 is the smallest of the bunch, and even that measures in at 4.8 liters. You'd think, then, that all V10s must surely have to be meaty by nature to work, but you'd be wrong. Say hello to the Connaught Type D concept: a sports car conceived in 2004 and equipped with a pipsqueak 2.0-liter V10. Yes, two liters.

Industry observers note that for some perspective, many passenger cars these days use 2.0-liter four-cylinder engines, including the Honda Civic hatchback, which is the platonic ideal of economy cars. Now imagine constraining yourself to such a small surface area, with the added complication of having to manage an extra six cylinders. The result would be ... amazing, actually.

It has been revealed that the standard Connaught used a naturally aspirated V10 and a Lynch electric motor for 162 hp. Yes, hybrid technology was being tested as far back as 2004 with this car, long before the hypercar Holy Trinity was formed and crowned. However, in the top-spec "Syracuse GT" version, the Type D's V10 engine was instead paired with a supercharger for a healthy 300 hp. The Connaught Type D Syracuse GT's 0 to 60 mph was projected to be in the low-four-second range, and popular publications cited a top speed of roughly 171 mph. This thing also tipped the scales at just 1,874 pounds.

Those are some serious numbers and would be enough to trouble many four-cylinder sports cars that, dare we say, could be called super. Even today's fleet of racey four-banger metal wouldn't be safe. The Honda Civic Type R, which is a rowdy teenage dirtbag, takes about a second longer to get to 60 mph, while the 2026 Ford Mustang RTR (with its 2.3-liter engine) only just edges it by two-tenths of a second (via Car and Driver). Unfortunately, the Type D never made it past the concept stage and into production due to funding concerns.

The brand was acquired in 2016 by a British automotive design company called Bevan Davidson International (BDI), and in 2021, it came up with a wild idea to revive Connaught with a 20-cylinder supercar called the X20. We'll give you a moment to rub your eyes and re-read the final part of that sentence.

Industry observers note that that 20-cylinder engine would be made up of two horizontally opposed and mid-mounted 2.0-liter V10s. It would also blow its waste gases out of no fewer than 20 exhaust pipes, rev all the way up to 10,000 rpm, and, as far as the firm's calculations go, produce more than 500 hp. That sounds less like a car, and more like a miniature steam train from the 17th century, but no word on whether any have been produced yet.

According to recent reports, whether BDI chooses to also bring the original Type D back to life remains to be seen, but just think about it for a second: A tiny-displacement, supercharged V10-powered sports car built to comply with the ever-growing regulations posed on the industry by lawmakers. Wouldn't that be just marvelous?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that XPENG just reported 3rd quarter financial details today, while also forecasting what will happen in the 4th quarter. Everything is looking quite rosy at the moment.

According to recent reports, as far as 3rd quarter financials go, on the back of strong sales, the manufacturer logged 24.28 billion yuan ($3.643 billion) of revenue. That’s a new quarterly record for the company. It’s 19% more than in Q3 2025 and 23% more than Q2 2026.

Industry observers note that that noted, despite strong revenue, the tech giant still scored a net loss. It had a significant 870 million yuan ($130.5 million) net loss, in fact, which was up 128% from 380 million yuan in Q3 2025 and down 35% from 1.34 billion from Q2 2026. XPENG made a small profit in Q4 2025, and since then has again been trying to get its finances into the green again instead of in the red.

Sources indicate that good news going into the 4th quarter is the organization expects even better. XPENG is forecasting 169,000 to 174,000 vehicle deliveries, which would mean year-over-year growth of 45% to 50%. Expected revenue is 30.4 billion yuan to 31.8 billion yuan, which would mean growth of 37% to 43%.

We’ll see. The manufacturer is still not expected to get another net profit quarter, but perhaps the quarter could surprise and XPENG could log its second quarterly profit. One thing making that unlikely, though, is that XPENG’s R&D costs were up significantly, 17.5%. Also, general and administrative expenses were up 11.4% year over year. We’ll see what the 4th quarter brings.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
Ardent Health acquiring Missouri nonprofit Boone Health for $47M" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Recent findings suggest that ardent Health is acquiring Boone Health, a mid-sized nonprofit system based in Columbia, Missouri, for $47 million in cash, the organizations confirmed Thursday. It marks Ardent's first entry into the Missouri healthcare market.

Recent findings suggest that the deal, expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, includes a 10-year, $200 million capital commitment on nonprofit Ardent’s part. That money will be invested in Boone’s facilities, workforce and, in the near term, an expansion of its emergency department, according to the announcement.

Sources indicate that ardent has agreed to maintain Boone’s essential hospital services while developing its 392-bed regional referral center, Boone Hospital Center. It also prepares to maintain employment for existing Boone employees and providers, continue its charity care policy and establish a local advisory board.

“We are acquiring a strong asset in an attractive and growing midsize market with significant opportunity to drive operating and financial improvement, all while delivering high patient quality care and safety,” Ardent Health President and CEO Dave Caspers stated during a Thursday afternoon investor call discussing the deal. “It also represents an effective use of capital at a compelling valuation that we expect will create long-term shareholder value.”.

It has been revealed that alongside its main hospital, Ardent would acquire Boone’s medical group, 19 care sites including an outpatient campus and five medical office buildings, related ancillary services and real estate. The system is the second-largest provider in its region with about 30% market share and half a billion dollars of annual revenue, Caspers noted, with a local population that is well insured (93% coverage) and growing well ahead of the national average (3.4% in the next five years).

“Boone expands our footprint into a fresh attractive market,” Caspers explained. “It diversifies our business and enhances scale. Further, adding Boone's regional system to our portfolio is consistent with our strategy of building leading healthcare platforms in growing mid-sized communities. We're highly aligned with Boone Health on culture and mission, including putting the patient at the center of everything we do, with an aim toward best-in-class clinical care, patient quality, safety and access to services.”.

Industry observers note that the executive noted to investors that Boone’s facilities are relatively modern and well maintained, allowing Ardent to direct more capital toward its growth. The manufacturer has also identified “meaningful opportunities to optimize financial performance.” By leveraging its larger scale and expertise to tackle costs (supply chain procurement, vendor consolidation) and revenue cycle processes, Ardent executives mentioned they expect to generate about $5 million to $10 million additional EBITDA within the deal’s first year, and at least $30 million of annual synergies three years after the deal’s close.

Boone Health has been independent since 2021, following over three decades during which it operated as part of the BJC HealthCare system. In 2025, its leadership kicked off a search for potential strategic partners “that could provide additional capital and resources to support the system's continued growth. Ardent was selected after a comprehensive evaluation process led by an independent advisory firm,” according to Thursday’s announcement.

According to recent reports, “In Ardent, we identified a partner that supports our mission, respects our culture and can accelerate our vision without compromising what makes Boone Health special,” Jerry Kennett, M.D., chair of Boone’s Board of Trustees, noted in the announcement. "Following a thoughtful review, the Board is confident Ardent is the right long-term partner for Boone Health. This agreement protects what our community has built while giving Boone Health the resources it needs to grow.".

Ardent Health’s current operations include 30 acute care hospitals and over 280 care sites, several of which are run as part of a joint venture structure with other health system partners. In 2025, the company increased its revenues by 6% to $6.3 billion and grew its adjusted EBITDA to $545 million.

Recent findings suggest that the company recently logged a strong third quarter off the back of solid demand for emergent care and progress on its ongoing performance improvement initiative. In September, it also officially divested from a joint venture with the University of Kansas Health System, a decision that leadership remarked is part of an ongoing review of its portfolio to ensure long-term strategic fit among its hospitals and partnerships.

Industry News: 2027 Toyota GRMN Corolla Cranks The GR's Fun Factor Up To 11

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1164 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Toyota shook up the compact performance car space when it introduced the GR Corolla back in 2022, and perhaps even more remarkably, it has continuously improved the car each year since.
  • In a recent development, that comparison showed me how the GR team's gradual tweaks positively impacted the experience of driving a GR Corolla, and last week I got the chance to try out their latest creation.
  • It has been revealed that full disclosure: Toyota wanted me to sample an array of its latest offerings for 2027 so badly that it flew me out to Texas, put me up in a hotel for a few nights, and kept me fed so I could drive its cars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota shook up the compact performance car space when it introduced the GR Corolla back in 2022, and perhaps even more remarkably, it has continuously improved the car each year since. I had the distinct pleasure of hucking the 2026 GR Corolla around Sonoma Raceway last year at the press launch, and in a rare turn of events, I actually got to compare its driving dynamics to a 2025 car as well as a 2024 model.

In a recent development, that comparison showed me how the GR team's gradual tweaks positively impacted the experience of driving a GR Corolla, and last week I got the chance to try out their latest creation. Toyota let me loose the limited-production 2027 GRMN Corolla around Eagles Canyon Raceway in Texas to experience what is the ultimate Corolla — for now, at least. Again, the changes are small, but the resulting improvements are immediately palpable.

It has been revealed that full disclosure: Toyota wanted me to sample an array of its latest offerings for 2027 so badly that it flew me out to Texas, put me up in a hotel for a few nights, and kept me fed so I could drive its cars. I only got to drive the GRMN Corolla on the track, so I cannot offer on-road impressions.

Recent findings suggest that the GRMN Corolla earned those last two letters while lapping arguably the most iconic race track on the planet, the Nürburgring. The MN in GRMN represents the fact that this version of the GR Corolla was tuned by the "Meisters of the Nürburgring," and that's not just marketing jargon. The GR team made suspension, aerodynamic, cooling, and drivetrain tweaks. They also swapped some metal body panels for carbon-fiber ones, all with the goal of making the GRMN Corolla the most track-focused GR Corolla yet.

In a recent development, suspension-wise, Toyota changed the bump stops because it found the GR Corolla's standard suspension would hit the bump stops on certain corners of the Nürburgring, causing sudden understeer. Aerodynamically, Toyota added a larger hood duct, bumper side splitters, fender ducts from the Super Taikyu hydrogen-engine GR Corolla development car to reduce front-end lift, and that adjustable rear spoiler for increased stability. The entire hood, both front fenders, and the rear spoiler are made from carbon fiber, and the rear seat was removed in order to save weight, making the GRMN weigh 66 pounds less than a standard GR Corolla.

Moving to the drivetrain, Toyota added a supplemental AWD transfer case oil cooler that will also be available for other GR Corollas but comes as standard on the GRMN, which keeps the system cool even after repeated laps in high temperatures. There's also a standard intercooler sprayer to keep it and the turbo working hard in high temperatures, too.

It has been revealed that engineers retuned Track Mode in the GRMN's GR-Four all-wheel-drive system to make it more rear-biased, and they managed to increase the turbocharged 1.6-liter three-cylinder engine's torque output by 7 pound-feet while also making maximum torque available at lower engine speeds, so it now produces 300 horsepower and 302 lb-ft. The changes are definitely palpable on the track, with my favorite upgrades being the GRMN's sticky Pilot Sport Cup 2 tires, the retuned steering rack with increased feedback, and the close-ratio transmission from the Morizo Edition, all of which heightened the GRMN Corolla's dynamics.

Industry observers note that toyota so graciously let the media go hog wild on Eagles Canyon Raceway before, which I had never seen or driven before, and luckily I was in the perfect car to attempt to learn the 2.7-mile "Italian Canyon" course's 15 corners, 20 apexes, and 150 feet of elevation change. We weren't allowed to do any consecutive laps — we had to enter the pits on each lap — but we were allowed to do as many laps as we pleased. I drove both the GRMN Corolla and a 2026 GR Corolla to see if I could tell the difference, and the answer was a resounding "hell yeah!".

In a recent development, taking off from the pits, the GRMN Corolla's inputs immediately felt more taut and communicative, from the snickety shifter to the talkative steering. Once I left pit lane and got to wring out the powertrain, the GRMN's extra mid-range torque and lighter weight made it feel like it had noticeably more shove than the standard GR. Cornering is where the GRMN really shined, though.

When I first entered a corner, the GRMN's reworked steering felt sharper and more direct, and the more rear-biased all-wheel-drive tune in Track Mode made its nose feel like it could change direction like a greyhound weaving through the slalom at the AKC National Agility Championship. Compared to the GR, the GRMN felt markedly more agile and more eager to rotate rather than understeer.

Sources indicate that the GRMN's retuned engine pulled its lighter weight out of corners stronger than the GR, and its Cup 2 tires made it cling to the road with what felt like merciless ferocity. Naturally, since this was my first time on this track I made my fair share of corner misjudgments, but even when I overcooked a decreasing radius turn, a dab of brakes made the GRMN dive toward the apex, expertly turning "oh crap" moments into drama-free learning experiences. Chief Engineer for the GR Corolla Naoyuki Sakamoto called the GRMN, "a car you can confidently push the limits in," and Sakamoto-san was absolutely correct.

The GRMN Corolla is an extremely limited-production vehicle, with just 730 units planned globally, so the U.S. market will get even fewer than that. Exclusivity paired with the GRMN Corolla's other driving experience enhancements and proven track-oriented capabilities make it a rare special edition that truly feels special. That noted, it's set to cost $65,665, so it had better be pretty damn special to make you pay $65k for a freakin' Corolla.

Sources indicate that the interior is all Corolla, but at least it has more aggressive bucket seats and a flocked instrument panel and A-pillars. You also forgo the opportunity to bring more than one passenger along for the ride, since the GRMN has what looks like a lap bar from a roller coaster rather than a back seat. Perhaps the biggest matter I had with the GRMN Corolla was that its rear windows do not roll down. The driver's window control panel has just two switches, one for the driver's side front door and one for the passenger side window, which I can imagine will cause horrendous wind buffeting for anyone who enjoys driving with the windows down.

It has been revealed that in case you couldn't tell, I was totally taken by the GRMN Corolla. I already loved driving the GR Corolla, but the GRMN Corolla's sharpened inputs, hardcore style, and delightful driving dynamics take that love even further. I truly hope this was not the last time I can drive one.

#18678. Industry News: BMW In South Carolina: A Free Trade Success Story

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2209 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy 📈 Bullish 🌐 Cleantechnica ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: BMW In South Carolina: A Free Trade Success Story

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2209 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, I recently attended BMW’s “Beyond The Machine” event in South Carolina.
  • Beyond the vehicles and manufacturing, which I plan to cover in more detail in future articles, one of the most striking aspects was the human impact.
  • Industry observers note that the area around Greenville, South Carolina the rose to prominence in the 1870s on the textile industry.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I recently attended BMW’s “Beyond The Machine” event in South Carolina. The largest facility of the German company globally is Plant Spartanburg in Greer, South Carolina. As part of the event, I saw the opening of BMW’s latest battery plant in nearby Woodruff. We stayed in the nearby city of Greenville, which was transformed by BMW and the businesses that followed.

Beyond the vehicles and manufacturing, which I plan to cover in more detail in future articles, one of the most striking aspects was the human impact. From the “Woodruffian” Mayor fighting back tears at the opening of the battery plant to the plant employees to the people I met exploring the town, they clearly appreciate what BMW has done for the community. Throughout the presentations and discussions, there was support for free trade along with the local benefits. People in the area pride themselves in their resilience. They have reason to be proud. And they were optimistic about the growth of the increasingly clean manufacturing and electrified products from this global company.

Industry observers note that the area around Greenville, South Carolina the rose to prominence in the 1870s on the textile industry. Cotton from throughout the South that had previously been shipped to other areas for processing was processed in Greenville and Spartanburg counties. However, as global competition increased in the 20th century, the mills became less competitive. The last textile mill closed in Greenville in 1977, although a few textile operations continued in the region into the 1980’s. As that industry left, the local economy declined. If the story ended there, many might use it as an argument against free trade.

When BMW came to South Carolina in 1992, they saw a lot of potential. Michelin had already started making tires there in 1978. Local leaders were enthusiastic to work with BMW. The people were also enthusiastic to receive training for the upcoming jobs. The deep-water port of Charleston on the other side of the state facilitated shipping, while nearby rail links connected to much of the US.

Industry observers note that since 1992, BMW has invested over $15.8 Billion. The latest Woodruff battery plant is their most recent major investment. In the process, an area that could have been considered a casualty of global trade became one of its greatest beneficiaries.

Industry observers note that the first model, an E36 3 series, rolled off the line in 1994. BMW also produced the Z3 in the plant, including the first “German” car driven by James Bond on camera. However, the big breakthrough came with the introduction of the X5 in 1999. At the time, relatively few SUVs were being sold in Europe. BMW Spartanburg as the center of SUV production was intending to largely for the US. However, global markets shifted.

Now, Spartanburg is the “Home of X.” It right now produces the X3, X5, X6, X7 and XM, including electrified versions. It is the sole manufacturing plant for a number of those SUV models globally. A little over half of their production is exported, which also makes it consistently the top US overseas automotive exporter. Export volume topped $9 Billion in 2025 over roughly 200,000 X vehicles.

Sources indicate that BMW designed those vehicles to be able to use ICE, PHEV and BEV powertrains. While some may want them to make just pure BEV, the approach gives BMW the ability to shift rapidly with the market. The different models also give the plant a level of market resilience. However, to fuel that resilience they need a very flexible supply chain that can respond quickly. Suppliers being close to the plant creates greater resilience.

BMW is designing its vehicles to be globally competitive. While 400+ miles of EPA range and charging speeds approaching 500 kW may be at the top of the US market, they are also competitive in global markets. While BMW developed the cells and packs, they use multiple suppliers to manufacture the cylindrical cells to their specifications. Packs at the plant right now use AESC cells, but they will shift to LG in the future and use other suppliers in other markets.

In a recent development, BMW also worked with the state of South Carolina to develop people. Nearby Clemson University provides a source of engineering talent, and BMW partners with the university on the Clemson University International Center for Automotive Research, where both students and BMW benefit from the development of latest innovations. They are also developing potential future suppliers with the BMW Venture funds. One such company will be supplying flax-based composites to future M models.

A heavy emphasis is placed on technical training at the factory. In addition, they collaborated with community colleges to provide technical training. But the development programs start much earlier, with a heavy emphasis in middle school and sponsoring the First Robotics Competition for elementary school students.

BMW also worked with the South Carolina Department of Transportation to build infrastructure to support the plant and its suppliers. Moving forward, that infrastructure will increasingly include electrification and EV charging. BMW also worked with the SC Ports Authority to develop an “inland port,” which is essentially a direct rail link to the Port of Charleston. By moving freight by rail, emissions are greatly reduced. In addition, a lot of emphasis is going into transferring freight quickly, as every minute a truck sits idling is also wasted emissions.

Recent findings suggest that while BMW employs 11,000 workers, over four times as many jobs are supported by the plant, according to a Clemson economist. That multiplier is much higher than most companies due to how BMW operates. Part of the impact on the local economy beyond employee count comes from the strategy behind the manufacturing. Overall, more than 70% of the value of the vehicles comes from outside suppliers.

Plant Spartanburg receives 3.3 million parts per day delivered by 1200 truckloads and 50 sea containers, 6 days per week. All those parts then go into over 1500 vehicles produced per day. The plant is laid out a bit different than some other manufacturing plants to facilitate the supply chain. Multiple fingers go up off the main line, along which parts are delivered to be assembled nearby. There isn’t much in the way of warehousing. Trucks come to the plant each day and the parts can end up on vehicles driving off the line the same day.

According to recent reports, in the initial stages of manufacturing, more of the supply base came from overseas. However, as the plant established itself, more suppliers localized. That growing supply chain then attracted additional companies to the region, like Mercedes, Volvo and Scout. Those companies then create greater scale for the suppliers, who can reduce costs and expand operations.

Overall, for heavy, bulky components, localization will tend to  happen naturally. For a company that relies on suppliers to consistently and almost constantly deliver parts, that localization tends to increase. The more localized the supply chain, the more capable it becomes to respond to market dynamics. Once scale is attained for heavy, bulky components like batteries, that production will naturally become more localized.

BMW has a growing supply chain footprint across the Americas and especially across the Southeastern US. There will be over 850 Tier 1 supplier locations in the Americas by 2027, with multiple times as many Tier 2 and Tier 3 suppliers providing materials, parts and components. BMW focuses on value creation, competitiveness and collaboration in their supply chain. In addition, while they are bringing economic benefit, they are also focused on decarbonization.

Of course, all this economic activity has brought “green” in terms of money to the local communities. As I was stranded in Greenville due to flight interruptions, I had time to walk around the town and speak to some of the locals. Streets that were once desolate and unsafe are now vibrant with shops and restaurants. An area that people once wanted to leave is now growing rapidly and attracting people from around the world. I started conversations  with several friendly people in town about trade. I heard stories of transformation from past struggles to current successes.

Sources indicate that even though it was clear that they were benefitting from the economic impact, I was still surprised how strongly and openly they supported free trade and realized the benefits. A local guide pointed out major buildings and businesses that were new. Downtown is now pleasant and walkable. Part of that is due to the restoration of a river that runs through the city, surrounded by shops and artwork, where I saw some locals fishing in the clear water. This gets to the other kind of “green.”.

While there are a lot of trucks transporting materials and components, shortened travel distances and efforts to streamline intermodal transfers reduce emissions. The proximity enables packaging to typically be sent back to the supplier to be reused. BMW is also putting a lot of effort into reduced CO2 emissions steel produced locally, which I plan to follow up on. Over half the steel in their vehicles is reduced CO2. Solar panels and landfill gas provide power for their facilities.

As the company relies heavily on its supply chain, the supply chain is a major focus of its decarbonization strategy. While EVs reduce emissions overall, the proportion of emissions from the manufacturing phase tends to be higher than for ICE vehicles, adding emphasis to decarbonization of manufacturing. At the same time, they strive to create regional strength, resilience and value creation while reducing emissions. Close collaboration is the key to meeting these goals. BMW plans to have net zero CO2 emissions throughout their supply chain by 2050 at the latest.

The new Woodruff plant will produce their sixth-generation battery. BMW develops the batteries first and then outsources the cell manufacturing, but they will now be manufacturing the packs locally. Initially, this will be for the iX5, to be delivered domestically and to global markets. However, additional EV models may benefit in the future.

Industry observers note that overall, politicians in the 1970’s could have tried to block global competition to protect the textile mills. That might have extended the life of those plants for a few years. However, in the process, those plants would become less globally competitive and less globally relevant. Protectionism would have only extended a slow, painful decline.

However, by keeping the market open and staying open to upcoming business opportunities, Greenville, Greer, Spartanburg and Woodruff created the circumstances for their current success. People were open to new companies from other countries. They were open to industries that were new to the area. And they were open to investing in retraining to better take advantage of the new opportunities.

Industry observers note that in the initial site selection, South Carolina could have imposed strict regulations and tried to force localization before the factory was built, production was ramped up and scale was attained to support that localization. If that happened, the plant would have undoubtedly been built elsewhere, and the economic benefits would have gone to someone else. By taking a more collaborative approach, rather than being confrontational, both BMW and local suppliers benefitted greatly. Building on that approach, more companies came to the region, building scale and amplifying the benefits.

BMW is not being hypocritical in their support of free trade. They are not promoting free trade just when it benefits them and then putting up barriers for other competitors. They are not shying away from global competition. They are seeking to make globally competitive vehicles for global markets. While global competition is fierce, by facing that competition, rather than hiding from it, their products become more competitive.

In the process, one of the brightest spots in US automotive trade globally, as well as one of the leaders in electrified product and supply chain decarbonization, comes from a German company.

Change and globalization can be scary things. Especially in the short term. The transition to EVs can also be scary, especially for those tied to the past. However, hiding behind political and trade walls rarely works out in the long run. A willingness to be open and collaborative with people who might come from within different lines on a map or sound different than you can have long term benefits. And the courage to engage with the technology transition and compete globally can put you ahead of many established competitors. That cannot only transform how we power our vehicles, but also transform the lives of people in communities for generations to come. As Woodruff Mayor Kenneth Gist put it at the battery plant opening:.

According to recent reports, BMW and the City of Woodruff wanted the same thing. Success in business, success in our community, and success in building the next generation of BMW electric vehicles to be the best in the world….

…When I think about this plant, I think about our children, our grandchildren. Educational partnership that will open the doors for them, the career that will be waiting for them, and a Woodruff they would be proud to call home for decades to come. BMW, you have been a true partner to me personally, to every person in this community.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Analysts at consulting firm Numerof & Associates released their 2027 outlook report for the insurance industry, and said that in a world where the cost of healthcare continues to rise, more patients and strategy sponsors are asking questions about what intends are bringing to the table.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
Plan sponsor expectations, policy shifts set to pressure payers in 2027" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

2027 is shaping up to be a complex year for health aims, as demands from clients to demonstrate value get louder, according to a new report.

Analysts at consulting firm Numerof & Associates released their 2027 outlook report for the insurance industry, and said that in a world where the cost of healthcare continues to rise, more patients and strategy sponsors are asking questions about what intends are bringing to the table.

It has been revealed that increasing transparency makes it easier for members to make their own healthcare decisions, but that alone isn't enough to resolve affordability challenges, per the report. It means that insurers will be tasked with engaging differently with consumers and transforming their experiences.

It has been revealed that "The bigger problem is not just that healthcare costs keep rising, but the traditional insurance model is becoming increasingly tough to sustain without demonstrating better value," noted Michael Abrams, co-founder and managing partner at Numerof, in an interview. "Consumers and employers are getting more sensitized to the issue of value.".

That interest in finding greater value is pushing employers to consider alternative models and approaches that can manage benefit costs, such as direct provider contracting, onsite clinics and care navigation programs.

According to recent reports, the expectation is not just lower costs, but to drive better outcomes and have greater accountability over the medical benefit offerings, per the report. And this trend opens the door for fresh entrants to thrive and challenge the role of health looks as the bridge between employers and providers.

Abrams stated digital health companies that target certain specialty areas, such as musculoskeletal care or diabetes, have a significant opportunity to fill that gap.

"These digital healthcare companies aren’t necessarily replacing insurers; they’re competing for functions that insurers traditionally performed or should be performing," he mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that in addition, these trends are gaining steam at a time of significant policy upheaval, further complicating the outlook for health intends, according to the report. The expiration of the enhanced premium tax credits for Affordable Care Act plans has driven up costs, and Medicaid work requirements taking effect on Jan. 1 could significantly grow the uninsured or underinsured population.

Reimbursement trends in other markets, such as Medicare Advantage, are also in the mix, the report said.

Abrams said the "convergence" of those policy changes with increased pressure from clients and members makes for a uniquely challenging combination.

"Insurers are getting squeezed from a number of different things all at the same time," he stated.

The report recommends that looks looking to survive in this complex time should focus on demonstrating their value to initiative sponsors and enrollees, particularly around managing the total cost of care. Insurers should also rethink how they engage with members to support a stronger relationship with consumers.

Recent findings suggest that it also means finding ways to think differently about their relationship with providers; a step that will be critical to addressing the cost of care. Payers should look for provider partners that can take on risk, and work proactively with providers to drive better outcomes and improve value.

According to recent reports, abrams noted that payer-provider dynamics are often coercive rather than collaborative. In one market, the insurer may be more powerful and in another, the provider, but in either case, it's based around a show of dominance rather than working together.

"With continued consolidation on both sides, we have seen a kind of polarization where the only mechanism for resolution is who has the biggest market clout," Abrams said.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Over the course of the five-week trial, her defense team sought to convince jurors that Clancy should not be held legally accountable for the killings because of a "lack of criminal responsibility," according to the Boston Globe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lindsay Clancy is set to face a second murder trial on March 29, 2027—less than one year after her first case ended in a hung jury and more than three years after she was accused of murdering her three children inside the family's Massachusetts home.

Clancy, 36, has admitted to taking the lives of her daughter, Cora, 5, and sons Dawson, 3, and 8-month-old Callan, but has pleaded not guilty to the three first-degree murder charges against her, with her attorneys arguing that she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis at the time of their deaths.

Over the course of the five-week trial, her defense team sought to convince jurors that Clancy should not be held legally accountable for the killings because of a "lack of criminal responsibility," according to the Boston Globe.

Following 19 hours of deliberation, the 12-person jury was declared deadlocked after telling state Judge William Sullivan it was unable to reach a unanimous verdict. Sullivan instructed the jurors to return to the deliberation room and continue their efforts to reach a verdict, before eventually declaring a mistrial.

Then, mere weeks ago, Clancy returned to court, where her legal team attempted to argue that she can't be retried due to double jeopardy in hopes to have the charges dropped. Meanwhile, the prosecution asked the judge to decline the motion to dismiss the charges, claiming they could have a retrial.

Now, it has been revealed that the prosecution will be retrying Clancy on the same charges, with pretrial hearings scheduled for Dec. 30 and Feb. 18.

Sources indicate that clancy's attorney, Kevin Reddington, previously claimed that he was ready to begin the retrial as soon as possible. He also requested President Donald Trump pardon Clancy; however, presidents can only pardon federal offenses.

Though Clancy was present in the courtroom in Plymouth, MA, she did not testify during the trial, which featured sworn testimony from dozens of witnesses, including her former husband, Patrick Clancy, medical professionals who treated her for mental health issues, and a former nanny who looked after her children.

Sources indicate that the former nurse accused several medical providers of malpractice and negligence, claiming that she was repeatedly misdiagnosed, even as her symptoms continued to worsen. On the night of Jan. 24, 2023, she reportedly experienced suicidal hallucinations and heard a voice telling her that it was her "last chance" to kill herself and her children.

The prosecution, however, argued that she wasn't diagnosed with postpartum depression and that the murders seem premeditated, calling attention to the fact that Clancy had reportedly looked up ways to murder on her cellphone prior to the deaths of her children.

While her husband, Patrick, was picking up a takeout meal, Clancy strangled her children and tried to take her own life by cutting her neck and wrists, then throwing herself out of her bedroom window at the family's Duxbury, MA, home.

Cora and Dawson were pronounced dead that same night, while Callan died in the hospital a few days later. Lindsay survived her injuries, but was left paralyzed from the waist down.

Clancy's husband took to the stand to testify on behalf of his wife—as did the couple's former nanny, Elaine Rossi, who described the former nurse as a "wonderful mother.".

In a recent development, "I observed a wonderful mom who loved her kids," the nanny stated, according to NBC10 Boston. "She cared for their safety, she was very concerned with Callan's eating and sleeping. She was a wonderful mother.".

Rossi also told the court that Clancy had revealed to her she was "suffering from postpartum.".

Patrick previously spoke out about his wife's horrifying crimes, sitting down with The New Yorker in October 2024 to defend her against critics, insisting that she was not "a monster.".

At the time of the interview, the father of three explained that he had since relocated from Massachusetts to an apartment in Fresh York City, quietly selling off the family's Duxbury home in an off-market deal.

In the interview, Patrick insisted that he "wasn't married to a monster," explaining how his wife had been suffering from anxiety and insomnia, which were brought on by her pregnancy with Callan.

Sources indicate that weeks before the terrible tragedy, he remarked, she had been hospitalized before being sent home with antidepressants. Despite all this, he said that he believed that her only diagnosis was a generalized anxiety disorder.

“I wasn’t married to a monster—I was married to someone who got sick,” he told the publication, adding that he had chosen to speak out to prevent further "lies and misinformation" from being spread.

Shortly after the deaths of his children, Patrick had issued a personal statement in which he asked the public to forgive his wife.

"A lot of people have said they can’t imagine and they’re right, there’s absolutely nothing that can prepare you," he wrote in the statement, which was shared on a GoFundMe page set up by his loved ones.

"The shock and pain is excruciating and relentless. I’m constantly reminded of them and with the little sleep I get, I dream about them on repeat. Any parent knows, it’s impossible to understand how much you will love your kids until you have them.

"The same goes for understanding the devastation of losing them. Cora, Dawson, and Callan were the essence of my life and I’m completely lost without them.

"My family was the best thing that ever happened to me. I took so much pride in being Lindsay’s husband and a dad to Cora, Dawson, and Callan. I always reminded myself that each day with them was a new gift.".

He then shared touching tributes to each of his children, calling attention to his favorite things about them, including son Dawson's "bold, brown eyes" and daughter Cora's "infection laugh.".

However, despite his grief, Patrick insisted that he had forgiven his wife, while urging the public to do the same.

"I want to ask all of you that you find it deep within yourselves to forgive Lindsay, as I have," he continued.

"The real Lindsay was generously loving and caring towards everyone—me, our kids, family, friends, and her patients. The very fibers of her soul are loving. All I wish for her now is that she can somehow find peace.".

While the Clancy family home does not appear to have been listed for public sale since the tragic events unfolded inside it, Patrick revealed to The New Yorker that he had, in fact, sold it to an anonymous buyer, adding during the interview that he'd just been informed the sale has officially closed.

It has been revealed that “There’s no house anymore,” he noted. “There are no kids. All that’s left is me and Lindsay.”.

He explained that he cleared out the house shortly after taking a solo trip to Central America and Europe in February 2024. He drove around his neighborhood gifting his children's stuffed animals and unused arcade cards to their friends.

Industry observers note that built in 1972, the home has been updated with refinished hardwood floors, a newer roof, and a redone kitchen with granite counters and latest appliances and flooring. The three-bedroom, 1.5-bath interior spans 1,732 square feet with a remodeled extra room between the garage and kitchen.

Recent findings suggest that the home sits on a tree-lined lot on almost an acre, with a deck, stone patio, and grassy lawn. The coastal town offers an "acclaimed" school system and a beautiful beach.

According to Realtor.com® records, the home last changed hands in 2018 for $500,000.

Driving The Scion By Toyota KEI-01 Will Make You Giggle And Jiggle In Places You Didn't Know Could Jiggle

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1173 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, I was just as shocked as you all were last week when Toyota declared the launch of the Scion by Toyota brand in the United States with a right-hand-drive kei truck.
  • Recent findings suggest that I was baffled by Toyota's choice to bring such a niche product in the United States, its choice to do so under the name "Scion by Toyota," and by its choice to make it available to fleets only.
  • Sources indicate that full disclosure: Toyota wanted me to sample a smattering of its newly introduced and updated models, so it flew me out to scenic Frisco, Texas, kept me fed and housed in a hotel for a few days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I was just as shocked as you all were last week when Toyota declared the launch of the Scion by Toyota brand in the United States with a right-hand-drive kei truck. The KEI-01 is limited to 25 mph in order to conform to low-speed vehicle (LSV) regulations, and as of now it's exclusively limited to fleet buyers. Though final details about the dinky little hauler remain slim, I did get a briefer-than-brief chance to whip around a prototype KEI-01 while attending the press event in Texas at which the truck was revealed, and the experience left me exceedingly tickled and slightly baffled.

Recent findings suggest that I was baffled by Toyota's choice to bring such a niche product in the United States, its choice to do so under the name "Scion by Toyota," and by its choice to make it available to fleets only. I was tickled by the opportunity to contort my comically long limbs in order to squeeze my 6-foot-8-inch tall body behind its wheel and take it for a spin. The result? A truly unique automotive experience that is all but guaranteed to make you giggle.

Sources indicate that full disclosure: Toyota wanted me to sample a smattering of its newly introduced and updated models, so it flew me out to scenic Frisco, Texas, kept me fed and housed in a hotel for a few days. I got to witness the announcement of the Scion by Toyota brand there, and drive the KEI-01 a few hundred feet.

The KEI-01 is not a brand fresh vehicle — in fact, it's based on the Toyota Pixis Truck, which is a rebadged 10th-generation Daihatsu HiJet Truck that itself was introduced 12 years ago now. We are only getting the "extended cab" version of the kei truck, generously called the Jumbo on the Daihatsu HiJet, which adds a taller roof and about an iPhone's length of room behind the two seats for storage — I used that space to store my shoes, since I couldn't fit behind the wheel while wearing them.

In its U.S. specification, the dinky KEI-01 will only be offered with a mid-mounted 660cc three-cylinder engine that sends its power to all four wheels via a CVT automatic transmission. Toyota didn't make power figures public, but it's almost certainly the same 660cc three-cylinder used in the other kei trucks that share the platform, which produces about 50 horsepower and 47 lb-ft of torque. The standard four-wheel-drive system features a lock mode that should make this little pickup rather capable on unpaved roads, but that's only if your spine is up to the task.

Sources indicate that they will all come standard with a weird mix of modern and throwback features, like dual front airbags, automatic emergency braking, push-button start, traction control, parking sensors, and an engine start/stop system. The standard climate controls are operated using horizontal levers like the ones in my grandfather's 1991 F-150, and the overall appearance of the interior looks like it belongs in a car that's being shown at Radwood, minus the significant tacked-on infotainment screen. I didn't get to experience any of these technology features on my abridged drive, except the start/stop system that I instantly turned off because it cut the AC and was unsurprisingly annoying.

Sources indicate that this was my first time driving a kei car, and I solely got to drive the KEI-01 on a short gravel loop, but the instant I started moving I was aware that it was not a refined vehicle. The suspension that gives it a 600-pound payload capacity also felt like it faultlessly transmitted even the smallest surface detail of every single piece of gravel I drove over directly to my butt. It jiggled parts of me that I didn't know could jiggle, and sounded very crashy going through dips and bumps. I wouldn't want to ride in one if I had a bad back. Though Toyota didn't release a spec sheet for the KEI-01, the Daihatsu Hijet has a truly puny wheelbase of 74.8 inches and laughably small tires, so no one should expect it to ride like a limousine.

As for its powertrain, the three-cylinder engine and CVT combination were more than enough to get the KEI-01 to its top speed of 25 mph, but the truck I drove did not have the limiter yet, so I saw as high as 40 mph. The CVT created a typical momentary lag between throttle pedal inputs and actual engine response, but discussing powertrain responsiveness in a kei truck that'll be limited to 25 mph is about as useful as discussing a upcoming hyperpop album with an octogenarian.

According to recent reports, if you didn't catch it upon first mention, I'm 6-foot-8, so I drew a bit of a crowd when I first tried inserting myself into the KEI-01. I'm all legs with a 40-inch inseam, and my first entry attempt was foiled by the immovable steering wheel. Once I took my shoes off and swung my left knee under the wheel first, I was able to finagle myself into a comfortable driving position, with about an inch left between my right knee and the hard plastic cupholder.

According to recent reports, headroom in the KEI-01 was downright impressive, though. Using the automotive industry's standardized headroom measurement, I had room to put one, maybe even two magician's hats on top of my head and still fit comfortably in the KEI-01. The cargo bed strangely protrudes a bit into the cab space, so the floor of the extended cab's rear storage area sits at about the same spot where the rear side window ends. It's a diminutive and awkwardly shaped and accessed space, but it allows for a bit of seat recline and is better than nothing.

In a recent development, annoyingly, Toyota hasn't released pricing for the KEI-01 as of yet, but as we already know it will be limited to fleet buyers initially anyway, so it's not like anyone can go to a Toyota dealer and buy one off the lot. Car and Driver estimates that the KEI-01 will cost around $28,000, though, which would be a really tough sell. I love that American fleet buyers are getting access to a brand newly introduced genuine kei truck — especially one that's built in the U.S. — but I am left to grapple with the point of it, especially considering that anyone can go out and find a derestricted imported kei truck for a rather low price.

It has been revealed that the so-cute-it-hurts Fiat Topolino is another recently unveiled U.S.-bound LSV, and I think it makes more sense than the KEI-01 since it will mainly be a cheeky electric neighborhood runabout for rich people. Its only competition are golf carts, where the KEI-01 will compete with a sea of UTVs that have served U.S. campuses, ranches, and other all-terrain hauling needs for ages. Who knows, maybe the fleet market will fall in love with the KEI-01, jiggles and all.

Tech Report: The BLUETTI Apex 200 Expandable Portable Power Station — CleanTechnica Tested

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1281 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • BLUETTI continues to innovate, finding upcoming ways to move its portable power station technology into meaningful new formats that provide owners with additional capability, portability, and utility.
  • They recently reached out about a fresh stackable portable power station format based around the Apex 200 power station.
  • Disclaimer: BLUETTI provided the Apex 200, B300K, and a pair of solar panels to the author for the purposes of this review.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BLUETTI continues to innovate, finding upcoming ways to move its portable power station technology into meaningful new formats that provide owners with additional capability, portability, and utility.

They recently reached out about a fresh stackable portable power station format based around the Apex 200 power station. It packs in a meaningful 2.5 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of storage capacity by itself, but the real magic is that it was built to be modular and can be linked up with additional storage modules to be stacked underneath, connecting directly to the main unit.

Disclaimer: BLUETTI provided the Apex 200, B300K, and a pair of solar panels to the author for the purposes of this review.

This modular format is a game changer because it means you don’t need an installer to bolt 300 pounds of batteries to the wall of your house. Instead, you can order them in manageable formats and add more as you need them. Among other things, this capability allows the owner to assemble and disassemble the battery pack that meets their needs when they need it.

Industry observers note that if you’re heading out to camp for a week in your RV, you can grab an Apex 200 and one of BLUETTI’s B300K expansion batteries and bring 5.5 kWh of capacity with you on the road. When you get home from the trip, you can put them back into the garage and add that back into the battery capacity for your home.

Recent findings suggest that the BLUETTI Apex 200 serves as a head unit or master controller for the battery stack, while the other battery modules are effectively servants to it. For example, when you’re setting the unit up to charge from a wall outlet or from a set of BLUETTI’s solar panels, which can wire directly into the Apex 200 with MC4 connectors, you simply plug one set of connectors or one AC charging cable into the Apex 200 and it automatically balances the energy storage across however many additional battery packs are plugged into the unit.

That really simplifies the charging structure and allows you to use the battery exactly how you want to. If you want to just head to the park with two solar panels that are portable, you can do that and have a much more manageable power system, effectively bringing a mini-grid with you on the go.

According to recent reports, we tested the BLUETTI Apex 200 out on a wall charger and, much like most of the other portable power stations on the market, it effectively maxes out the capacity you can actually draw from a wall outlet, which is around 1,600 watts continuous. Even with the best charging cables, you’re going to notice some heat building up in the cable, and BLUETTI has made some concessions for this. The Apex 200 has a switch that allows you to select from different charging modes:.

Industry observers note that when it comes to solar, the BLUETTI Apex 200 can plug in to solar arrays through either an XT60 connector or the MC4 connectors that wire directly into the unit on the side. Between the MC4 connectors and the XT60 solar input, the unit can pull down 3,000 watts of solar, though you will need to make sure the voltage on your panels lines up with what each of the ports on the unit can handle. When we initially wired our two Bluetti 100-watt solar panels into the unit, we had them wired in parallel, which resulted in just 40 volts being pushed into the unit.

Stacking them in series gave us 80 volts, which pushed it over the minimum 60 volts for the MC4 connectors and allowed the BLUETTI Apex 200 to start charging from the panels. Pushing 2,000 watts maximum of solar power into a 5.5 kWh battery stack is going to take some time to get it charged up, but it’s easy to manage scaling the input power system up to an impressive 2,000 watts to really deliver some meaningful power.

The flexibility is pretty impressive, because it means you can dial the system in to exactly what you need, whether that’s bolting an array to the top of your RV or installing solar panels on the side of your house and then wiring them in a way that’s the most convenient for you.

BLUETTI also makes a larger B500K battery, so you can really pick and choose exactly the right level of storage that you need for your house and the right size battery packs that you want to be able to move around.

Industry observers note that the MC4 connectors for solar panels are a little bit troublesome on the BLUETTI Apex 200 because they require a special tool to release the locks that connect the male and female ends of MC4 connectors together. That means if you have your solar panels wired up and plugged into the unit, you’ll need an MC4 connector release tool to disconnect the solar panels from the Apex 200 before you move on. Alternately, you can wire the solar panels up through an XT60 connector, which is a simple plug-and-play adapter for lower voltage solar setups.

When it came time to use the stored power from the BLUETTI Apex 200 and the B300K battery pack, we had to pick up some more high-draw appliances to really put them the the test. We bought a 1,500-watt electric fireplace and 1,500-watt portable heater for a total draw of around 3,000 watts by. We also grabbed an an Instant Pot from the kitchen to pull a bit more juice from the battery stack.

Recent findings suggest that the BLUETTI Apex 200 handled both of the heaters running full blast without a problem. It shared a continuous power output capacity of 3,200 watts. This gets bumped to 3,600 watts when you attach a B300K extension battery. Beyond that, you can even pull a little bit more power, pulling peak usage up to 4,800 watts for a few seconds, because of its peak power handling capacity.

Recent findings suggest that keeping the larger heater unit attached, we added an Instapot to the the mix, and again the unit had no concerns no matter what power levels we used. It’s a solid stack with impressive stats that actually deliver when you need them to the most.

Recent findings suggest that BLUETTI has really built an impressive system here with the Apex 200 and its different expansion battery options. A single BLUETTI Apex 200 can be expanded up to 33.3 kWh, and they can even go bigger than that if you need something with more storage.

In a recent development, BLUETTI allows you to link three Apex 200 battery stacks together through their Hub 1 accessory for a total of just under 100 kWh of storage capacity. That can be accomplished by stacking three Apex 200s with a bunch of BLUETTI’s 5kWh B500Ks and then linking them all together through the Hub 1.

It’s a massive system that reveals BLUETTI isn’t just building products for a quick sale, but building a much more comprehensive, flexible storage system that you can build at home into the right configuration for your needs with components that act more like LEGO building blocks.

According to recent reports, the ability to wire in solar via XT60 connectors and MC4 connectors is exciting, giving homeowners even more options to produce power from the sun for them to run their lives on. The BLUETTI Apex 200 retails for $1,399 USD.

For more information about the BLUETTI Apex 200, the B300K, B500K expansion packs, or their solar panels, head over to their official website.

CommonSpirit Health logs $544M operating loss to begin its FY2027" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Industry observers note that commonSpirit Health kicked off its 2027 fiscal year with a $544 million operating loss as decreasing acuity, dampening payer mix and other expenses outpaced the large nonprofit’s strong volumes and improving operating efficiency, according to financial results for the quarter ended Sept. 30.

Sources indicate that that operating loss excludes $65 million non-routine special charges incurred by the health system—most notably severance costs and other fees tied to its strategic, multi-billion-dollar decision to end a long-term revenue cycle contract with Tenet Healthcare—during the quarter, and reflect a -5.3% operating margin. The system had reported a $396 million operating loss and -4% margin during the same period a year prior.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) was $77 million in the quarter, also a dip from the prior year’s $129 million.

“Our first-quarter performance reflects steady operational progress, even amid persistent cost and reimbursement headwinds, as patients continue to choose CommonSpirit for quality care,” Chief Financial Officer Michael P. Browning stated in a release.

CommonSpirit, already one of the country’s largest health systems, said it grew its quarterly operating revenue 5.3% year over year to $10.3 billion. The uptick included a 2.8% year-over-year increase in adjusted admissions as well as $165 million in net income from the California provider fee program, as opposed to no such benefit recorded the year prior. At the same time, the organization said that its revenues were affected by “revenue yield challenges” and increases in self-pay, Medicare and Medicaid among its payer mix—both complications cited in recent financial reports from other major health systems.

In a recent development, meanwhile, CommonSpirit’s operating expenses (before special charges) rose 6.6% year over year to nearly $10.9 billion. Much of the increase was tied to higher volumes as well as salary inflation, the latter of which came even as the organization improved its labor productivity (hospital full-time equivalents per adjusted admission decreased by 1.4%) and cut down its contract labor spend.

In a recent development, commonSpirit’s results also included $115 million of net nonoperating income, substantially less than the year before due to “market fluctuations” affecting its investment returns. That left a bottom-line net loss of $496 million for the quarter and, as of Sept. 30, 160 days of cash on hand.

Management, in the filing and an accompanying press release, noted that the quarter’s numbers land as the system continues to execute on a sweeping operating performance improvement plan. That effort includes work to boost volumes through a focus on its care network, revenue realization efforts surrounding denials and managed care negotiations, standardizing department staffing models to trim labor costs and potential service line rationalization “for those markets where performance is presently below requirements.”.

Industry observers note that “We are making deliberate, near-term investments to unify our electronic health record, enterprise resource planning and revenue cycle platforms, while advancing responsible AI adoption to strengthen our system for the long term,” Browning remarked. “Keeping patients at the center of everything we do requires disciplined expense management and fair, timely reimbursement for the care we deliver.”.

Sources indicate that “Financial sustainability is what makes our mission possible,” added President and CEO Wright Lassiter III in the release. “Through disciplined operations, we are supporting our team members, strengthening our ministry and protecting access to compassionate, high-quality care across the communities we serve.”.

It has been revealed that commonSpirit Health comprises about 2,600 care sites, including 132 hospitals, and more than 160,000 employees across 24 states. In the most recent fiscal year ended June 30, it reported $42.4 billion in total operating revenue and a $430 million operating loss (-1% operating margin) before special charges, an improvement from the prior fiscal year.

Latest Update: Groups Decry Trump EPA’s Decision to Grant Louisiana Oversight of Toxic Coal Ash

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (599 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Testing at all Louisiana coal plants found unsafe groundwater contamination.
  • — The Sierra Club, Earthjustice, and the Alliance for Affordable Energy Louisiana decried the Trump administration’s final decision today to put the State of Louisiana in charge of oversight of toxic coal ash waste.
  • Coal ash is generated when coal is burned, and massive quantities are stored at coal-burning power plants near Baton Rouge, Alexandria, and Shreveport.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Testing at all Louisiana coal plants found unsafe groundwater contamination.

BATON ROUGE, La. — The Sierra Club, Earthjustice, and the Alliance for Affordable Energy Louisiana decried the Trump administration’s final decision today to put the State of Louisiana in charge of oversight of toxic coal ash waste. The Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality (LDEQ) has repeatedly allowed coal plants to violate federal coal ash protections.

Coal ash is generated when coal is burned, and massive quantities are stored at coal-burning power plants near Baton Rouge, Alexandria, and Shreveport.

It has been revealed that at all three active Louisiana coal plants (Substantial Cajun 2, Brame Energy Center, R S Nelson), and the state’s one retired plant (Dolet Hills), monitoring data indicates that coal ash is contaminating groundwater at levels above federal safe drinking water standards. These toxic chemicals include arsenic, boron, cobalt, lead, lithium, radium, sulfate, and thallium. More than 61% of Louisiana’s population relies on groundwater for all or part of their drinking water supply.

“Louisianans know all too well that we can’t trust our state regulators to hold polluters accountable, so it’s nonsensical that the Trump Administration just gave LDEQ even more authority to handle something as dangerous as coal ash,” noted Darryl Malek-Wiley, a Sierra Club senior field representative in Louisiana. “It’s clear this decision is meant to favor wealthy coal-owning utilities at the expense of our health.”.

In a recent development, “The Trump administration chose polluters over the people of Louisiana,” mentioned Earthjustice senior attorney Mychal Ozaeta. “An alphabet soup of toxic chemicals from burning coal is contaminating groundwater in locations across the state. The right thing to do is make the polluters clean up their toxic mess, and protect sources of drinking water. Instead, the Trump administration is handing over authority to Louisiana’s state government which won’t lift a finger to clamp down on the concerning levels of contaminants poisoning the state’s groundwater.”.

It has been revealed that “Our state regulators are dangerously inadequate in their oversight and enforcement of polluting industries, which has already cost Louisiana our safe air and water. We simply don’t think LDEQ can handle even more responsibilities they won’t take seriously,” noted Logan Burke, Executive Director of the Alliance for Affordable Energy.

Public interest groups submitted formal comments to EPA urging the administration to reject Louisiana’s request to handle coal ash oversight in the state.

Coal ash contains arsenic, mercury, chromium, lead, lithium, radium, and other heavy metals, which have been linked to numerous types of cancer, heart and thyroid disease, respiratory illness, reproductive failure, and neurological harm.

As an example of the state’s abysmal track record on coal ash, LDEQ has allowed power plants to close coal ash dumps with ash in groundwater, ensuring that the dumps will contaminate groundwater with toxic chemicals indefinitely. LDEQ should not be in charge of issuing permits that let coal plants continue to violate the law. These permits will shield power plants from federal enforcement and prevent Louisiana residents from stopping coal ash pollution.

Industry observers note that LDEQ is a severely understaffed and extremely lenient environmental regulator. In addition to its coal ash failures, its air monitors are far away from Louisiana’s heaviest air-polluting facilities, and the agency has for years been criticized for approving permits for wealthy polluters, including LNG terminals and a massive Formosa plastics factory. Louisianans know all too well that LDEQ does not protect low-income communities of color, and creates a lax regulatory environment that has enabled disasters like the recent Smitty’s Supply explosion and spill.

Please see the Earthjustice Louisiana coal ash page.

That's some dedication, and the car shows the love they obviously had for it. We'll have to decide if we love the price the current owner has set for its sale.

At some point in one's life, it's best to take the road less traveled. The well-beaten path may be the safest, but the less popular way might just offer unexpected, memorable adventures. The 2004 Nissan 350Z we looked at on Monday is probably not everyone's first choice when it comes to used sports cars with a semblance of panache. The easy answer is Porsche's Boxster or a Mazda Miata, but that's part of what makes the 350Z such a rogue option.

Capable and seemingly in as-upcoming condition, our 350Z came with a six-speed stick, a top that drops, and a $12,500 asking price. That's plumb right in the middle of 986 Boxster territory, but offering more power and potentially cheaper running costs. That concept didn't escape you all. Comments on the car ranged from "not for me, but a good deal for someone," to "if it were closer to me..." In the end, the vote went the Nissan seller's way, too, earning the Z a solid 76% 'Nice Price' win.

Nissan has never offered a mid-engine car for sale here in the States. In fact, of the major Japanese manufacturers, only Toyota and Honda (through Acura) have gone the (rear) mid-engine route here.

It has been revealed that in the early 1960s, mid-engine layouts were all the rage in racing, with F1, Indy, and GT classes moving to place the driver ahead of the drivetrain. Britain's Lotus was at the forefront of this movement, debuting the mid-engine Type 18 Formula 1 racer in 1960. That car brought Lotus its first F1 checkered flag and World Champion title.

Lotus also dallied with mid-engine GT racers, designing a chassis and body that the company hoped would be bought by the Ford Motor Company (Lotus had a close relationship with Ford at the time) for the Americans' assault on Le Mans. Ford chose the already race-tested Lola Mk 6 chassis for its GT40 racing program, leaving Lotus with significant engineering expense and little to show for it. Instead of initially building a race car from the proposed chassis, Lotus took the more lucrative route and built a road car: Hethel's first mid-engined model.

Industry observers note that the resulting Europa leveraged a design first used on the Elan: a stiff, folded and welded center backbone with the drivetrain and suspension bolted in place, and a fiberglass body mounted atop that in saddlebag fashion. The earliest cars had Renault engines and transmissions, while later cars, like this 1973 Europa Special, used the Ford Kent-based Lotus Twin Cam engine.

Not only does this Europa have the most powerful engine offered in Federalized form, but that 115-horsepower 1,557cc four-cylinder is backed by a standard five-speed manual, still sourced from Renault, originally designed for the French manufacturer's 16 model.

This isn't just a "Massive Valve" (denoting a reworked twin-cam head) Europa; it's also one of 100 John Player Specials built to commemorate Lotus's 1972 F1 Championship win. The cars were wrapped in black paint with gold trim, emulating the cigarette pack design of the racer's sponsor, Nottingham, England's John Player & Sons. It's an iconic bit of 1970s chic, and very British. This car still wears its commemorative dashboard plaque, indicating it's number 90 of the 100 cars built.

While the basic Europa design is a bit odd with its bread van back end, this one appears to be in exceptional condition. Also, being a later edition (dubbed Type 47 by Lotus), it has a reworked engine cover and rear end providing better visibility out the back and slightly improved proportions.

Sources indicate that not only does this Europa appear to be in near-show car condition, but it comes with extensive documentation from the moment it was built (March 1973) to the present day. That paperwork details title transfers between all three owners (the second owner held on to the car for more than half a century), along with all the work that has gone into keeping it on the road and winning awards at car indicates. As far as turnkey classics go, there's not much to complain about with this Lotus.

It has been revealed that on the exterior, the black-and-gold color scheme still looks as elegant as ever, right down to the original gold anodized alloy wheels. All the badging, lights, and chrome are present and in excellent shape, which is a plus since parts are getting increasingly hard to find. The interior is just as nice, showing just some scuffing on the driver's seat side as evidence of the car's age.

According to recent reports, according to the ad, the engine underwent an extensive rebuild and documentation just 2,000 miles ago, and now runs well when warm. Both the engine and gearbox are numbers-matching for the car. How cool is that after all these years?

Recent findings suggest that the ad notes a clean title and mileage documented at 34,526. It also touts the car as a "once in a lifetime chance to own a fully documented Lotus." It should be noted that, while advertised in the Los Angeles Craigslist classifieds, the car is actually located a few hundred miles away on the California/Oregon border.

Recent findings suggest that some classic cars come with a story. Some come with a past veiled in mystery. This Europa comes with a dossier that would make a CIA agent proud. Not only that, but it's a prime example of a significant model in its final, some might argue, most desired form. What might something like that be worth?

The seller has set a price of $27,000, and since the ad for the car has been posted for almost a month, we now need to give that asking price some thought. What's your take on this original mid-engined marvel out of Hethel and the seller's cash-and-carry price? Is it really worth $27,000? Or is a fairer price yet to be documented in the car's records?
