  • The singer, who shares the twins with ex-husband Marc Anthony, admitted that she "cried for six months straight" when her twins headed off to college.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jennifer Lopez has admitted that she is enjoying the "freedom" that comes with living alone after her 18-year-old twins, Max and Emme, left their California home for college.

The 57-year-old singer and actress—who is attempting to sell her and ex-husband Ben Affleck's $50 million marital mansion—once again opened up about the realities of being an empty nester while appearing on "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon.".

The singer, who shares the twins with ex-husband Marc Anthony, admitted that she "cried for six months straight" when her twins headed off to college.

Although Lopez confessed it has been "emotional," she insisted it has also been an "amazing" journey.

“It’s all the feelings. It’s like one of those moments in life where you’re just, you’re sad, you’re melancholy, but you’re excited and you’re hopeful—there’s just so many feelings that go with [it]. I cried for, like, six months straight, like, two months before they graduated until I dropped them off and then a few weeks after that," she noted.

Sources indicate that “It’s crazy ... like, I still have on my phone them on my lap, as babies," she added. "It goes so fast, just like everybody says.”.

The A-lister admitted that she is now getting comfortable with the "freedom" she has living alone.

It has been revealed that “It’s the first [time] since I was, I don’t know, in my early 20s that I haven’t been with someone, had my kids. I’m alone, I’m free—I can do whatever the f--- I want! And it’s kind of amazing, but also weird," she joked.

In October, Lopez mentioned she was channeling that “devastation” into her music.

Speaking to Variety, the hitmaker revealed that living alone has inspired a burst of songwriting, producing material she believes could become some of her biggest hits.

It has been revealed that “They take up such a major part of your brain for so long, and when they’re gone, which is devastating and sad and scary, you’re facing a life that’s totally different now, and you’re like, ‘What am I going to do with this space and this time?’" the hitmaker said. "For me, I just went back in the studio. I’ve written some of the best songs that I’ve ever written, and I’m really excited.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s a very happy-era album. It’s some of the most joyous, beautiful songs that have just a tad of a tear in them," she added.

Her comments come mere weeks after she got candid about her kids going off to college in an emotional social video.

"My kids are going away to college," she said while going through her morning skincare regimen.

The "On the Floor" singer revealed that she made a point of soaking up as much time as possible with Max and Emme over the summer, including traveling with them before they began their latest lives away from home.

Recent findings suggest that "I was thinking about this summer and what a great summer it was. We got to go away together. I spent as much time with them as I could," she recalled.

Lopez revealed she was facing the reality of returning to a much quieter home—and admitted that it hasn't been easy.

"When they go away and I'm sitting here being an empty nester, and crying and thinking about them and looking at baby pictures of them and all of that stuff, these routines are the things that are going to keep me kind of sane," she shared.

For Lopez, those routines include exercising, taking care of her skin, and making an effort to prioritize herself as she navigates the newfound free time that comes with having two college-age children.

"Working out, doing my skincare routine, caring for myself, with the newfound kind of space that's in your life," she said.

Industry observers note that but the superstar also acknowledged that the milestone comes with conflicting emotions. While she is thrilled to watch Max and Emme begin their adult lives, their departure also marks a major change for her.

"You're so excited for them to step into this new era of their life, but it's also, we have to remember, it's a new era of our lives, too," Lopez explained.

She encouraged other parents experiencing a similar transition to look at the change as an opportunity to reconnect with interests or ambitions that may have taken a back seat while raising children.

"Maybe it's time to revive some old dreams that you had," she suggested, adding that parents might return to something they "put aside during the time that you were raising your kids" or simply pursue activities they previously didn't have time for.

Still, Lopez didn't shy away from admitting that embracing such a significant lifestyle change can be daunting.

Industry observers note that "It's a scary time. It's a transitional time. It's a upcoming beginning, in a lot of ways, for them, certainly, but also for you," she noted.

She ended her message on an optimistic note, urging others entering the empty-nest phase to continue looking after themselves and finding purpose in their newly introduced routines.

"Keep your routines going. Stay hydrated. Stay happy, stay joyful, stay productive," she said. Lopez has been preparing for the milestone for months.

Earlier this year, she revealed during an interview with "Extra" that both Max and Emme had been accepted into all five colleges they applied to, with each also receiving a scholarship offer.

The proud mom also spoke about how hard the twins had worked to reach that point, explaining that both have ADHD and have had to find approaches to learning that work for them.

Lopez also made sure to carve out plenty of time with her children before their departure. Over the summer, she documented a road trip through Italy with Max and Emme.

Latest Update: Palo Alto Networks report finds organizations struggle to track and secure AI agents in the cloud

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1176 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A new report out today from cybersecurity company Palo Alto Networks Inc.
  • Now in its sixth year, the State of Cloud Security Report 2026 is based on a survey of 2,800 security executives and practitioners in 10 countries.
  • Recent findings suggest that the use of AI agents was found to be close to universal, with 99% of respondents saying they use agents for autonomous or semiautonomous actions in their development pipelines.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 08:00 EST / NOVEMBER 16 2026.

According to recent reports, A new report out today from cybersecurity company Palo Alto Networks Inc. finds that artificial intelligence agents have rapidly become a fixture in software development, but many organizations can’t properly track or secure what those agents are doing in the cloud.

Now in its sixth year, the State of Cloud Security Report 2026 is based on a survey of 2,800 security executives and practitioners in 10 countries. Along with how AI is being used to build and deploy software, the report looks at how quickly organizations are able to respond when something goes wrong.

Recent findings suggest that the use of AI agents was found to be close to universal, with 99% of respondents saying they use agents for autonomous or semiautonomous actions in their development pipelines. Some 73% said the agents are allowed to modify code, pipeline configurations or production environments, and agents are even doing security testing at 44% of organizations.

The amount of change is going up as a result. Some 82% mentioned AI-driven development has increased the volume of infrastructure updates reaching their cloud, yet organizations on average enforce fewer than three of the eight predeployment security checks measured in the survey. AI is also being used to generate infrastructure-as-code templates at 42% of organizations, but only 34% scan that code before production.

Not surprisingly, problems are getting through. Respondents said that on average, 19% of high and critical application security complications reached production over a 90-day period. It takes an average of 18.4 days to get a fix for a security problem found in code into production.

Sources indicate that when respondents were asked what was stopping them from fixing problems before deployment, the most common answer was business pressure to release swiftly at 39%. Unclear risk acceptance policies came second at 30%.

Sources indicate that accountability is also an issue when it comes to agents. Two in five organizations mentioned they are unable to reconstruct what an AI agent did, a share that rises to 46% in financial services, while 53% said agent activity is logged under a developer’s identity or personal access token. That means when something goes wrong, investigators first have to figure out which actions were taken by a person and which were taken by an agent before they can work out what was affected.

Removing access once something does go wrong is also slow. Some 60% of organizations still need manual intervention to revoke access for nonhuman identities, and it takes an average of 2.5 days to revoke or rotate compromised developer credentials, API keys or pipeline secrets.

Sources indicate that data governance has its own challenges. Nearly all organizations, 99%, said they had found ungoverned AI in their environment in the past year, yet only 9% are able to automatically discover and classify it. Some 40% said governed data had been copied into ungoverned AI tools, and 39% had seen sensitive or regulated data used to train or fine-tune models without authorization.

Recent findings suggest that despite the gaps, confidence is high. Almost every respondent, 97%, noted they are at least somewhat confident they can secure their AI supply chain and applications, though only 36% can monitor AI behavior in production and just 30% can detect prompt injection.

The final section of the report looks at the threat from frontier AI models that can find and exploit software vulnerabilities on their own. Nearly all respondents, 98%, said they are concerned about it, and 65% said it poses a significant or severe threat to global critical infrastructure and financial systems over the next 12 to 18 months. Utilities were the most likely of any sector to rate the threat as significant or severe at 79%, compared with 48% in telecommunications.

In a recent development, interestingly, though the report refers to “frontier AI-powered capabilities,” the survey questions at the back of it call them “Mythos-grade” threats, a reference to Anthropic PBC’s Claude Mythos models. Palo Alto Networks was one of the launch partners in Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, which gave defenders early access to Claude Mythos Preview in April.

The report argues that against attackers working at machine speed, an 18.4-day fix cycle leaves organizations exposed for more than 17 days after a vulnerability can be discovered. Part of the problem, according to the report, is fragmented tooling, with only 19% of organizations saying they operate with unified telemetry and workflows across code, cloud, identity and runtime. Nearly half of organizations, 47%, still do the work of correlating application vulnerabilities with runtime threats by hand, a number that’s even higher in the U.S. at 55%.

Recent findings suggest that the report ends with a series of recommendations for organizations to secure their cloud environments as AI agents take on more work. Agents should be given their own identities with a clear owner and only the permissions they need to do their job. Security teams are also advised to automate the fixing of recurring challenges, though only after rollback procedures have been put in place.

  • A home listing has always been good at telling you about a house: the square footage, the year it was built, the number of bedrooms.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 2026, Redfin added information about sunlight, weather, childcare access and more to home listings. Here is everything you need to know about what’s upcoming.

A home listing has always been good at telling you about a house: the square footage, the year it was built, the number of bedrooms. Historically, it has been less good at telling you what living there is actually like. Does the kitchen get morning sunlight? How hot are the summers? Is there a daycare within walking distance?

Those are the questions we set out to answer this year. Multiple new data sets arrived on Redfin in 2026, and they now sit alongside other information that was already there, including scores about a property’s walkability, transit access and climate.

Sunscore shows exactly how much sunlight a home gets.

Industry observers note that natural light is one of the hardest things to judge from listing photos or a single showing, and it matters more than you might expect. In a recent Redfin survey, nearly 70% of people said the amount of sunlight in their home affects their satisfaction with where they live, and 11% said it is non-negotiable when searching for a home.

Sunscore is a property-level rating from 0 to 100 that shows how much sunlight a home gets. We co-created it with Shadowmap, a sunlight analysis platform, using 3D modeling that tracks how shadows fall across a home throughout the day and across the seasons. Here are the score breakdowns:.

☀️ 90-100: Exceptional sunlight.

In a recent development, each score accounts for the home’s 3D shape and structure, surrounding buildings, trees and terrain, the sun’s position throughout the day, and seasonal changes across the year. In other words, it catches the things you would only discover after moving in—like a neighboring building that blocks the afternoon light in winter.

It has been revealed that and it is not only about comfort and aesthetics. A home’s sun exposure also states something about its solar potential, which can translate into real savings on energy costs over time.

Weather data helps predict precipitation and heat.

In a recent development, weather turns out to be one of the biggest reasons people move. In a recent Redfin survey conducted by Ipsos, 22% of Americans planning to move to another state said better weather was motivating the move—the most cited reason out of nearly 30 options, ahead of affordability, job opportunities and moving closer to family. Another 21% said concerns about climate change or natural disasters were shaping where they wanted to live.

According to recent reports, in July, we partnered with The Weather Company, owner of The Weather Channel app and weather.com, to bring historical weather data to every for-sale listing on Redfin. As our exclusive historical weather provider, it supplies the same data hundreds of millions of people check every month.

Each listing shows ZIP code-level averages for:.

Consider this information the difference between the weather on the day you tour a home and the climate you might actually live in.

Childcare data displays daycare and preschool options.

For families with young children, childcare access can determine a neighborhood’s fit as much as school boundaries do. However, it’s historically been missing from the home browsing experience. Redfin is the first major real estate portal to partner with Winnie, the largest marketplace for childcare and early education in the U.S., to bring local childcare information to for-sale listings.

Nearby daycare and preschool options now appear on for-sale home listings with details that determine whether a spot is realistic for your family, such as:.

Location scores capture everything from wellness access to noise.

While Walk Score, Bike Score and Transit Score already existed on home listings, Redfin has expanded these location scores to capture more information about a neighborhood’s vibe using Local Logic data.

Industry observers note that start exploring homes on Redfin.com or the Redfin app to learn everything you’d want to know about a property. Need a place to start? Use Redfin’s conversational search to begin your homebuying journey.

Bitcoin found its bottom? Bitcoin is fighting to hold $65,000 after a brutal weekend selloff pushed BTC USD below $62,000. The rebound offers bulls some relief, but the market is showing signs of a much deeper liquidity problem.

According to recent reports, the world’s largest crypto has lost 13% since the 8th of November, with Ethereum and XRP also hitting multi-month lows. Billions in leveraged positions have disappeared as traders rush to reduce exposure.

According to recent reports, yet the selloff has created an interesting setup. Extreme fear, forced liquidations, and heavily discounted prices could signal that much of the speculative excess has finally been removed.

The problem is that capital continues leaving the crypto market. Stablecoin supply has contracted for five consecutive weeks, while US spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded seven consecutive sessions of outflows.

Bitcoin now faces a defining question: has the market finally found its bottom, or is another crash waiting around the corner?

The latest liquidation wave has given the Bitcoin bottom argument some credibility. When leveraged traders are forced out, selling pressure can eventually exhaust itself, leaving the market with fewer speculative positions vulnerable to another cascade. What comes down must go up, and vice versa.

The weekend recovery also highlights that buyers are willing to defend the $62,000 region. BTC rebounded to $64,000 – $65,000 after briefly touching $62,006 this morning.

Market sentiment has also deteriorated sharply. Extreme fear is returning as investors abandon riskier positions and traders become increasingly defensive. This is often where market reversals begin. Sellers who wanted to exit have already sold, while longer-term investors start looking for attractive entry points.

Galaxy Research has also presented a bullish argument. In an October 26 report, the firm said it believed Bitcoin’s bottom was already in, pointing to diminished selling pressure, reduced speculative positioning, and stronger long-term fundamentals.

However, a convincing recovery needs more than a short-lived bounce. Bitcoin must attract fresh spot demand and reclaim vital resistance levels before bulls can claim victory.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026.

It has been revealed that the biggest obstacle to a Bitcoin bottom is the lack of fresh money entering the market. Stablecoin supply has contracted for five consecutive weeks. Glassnode puts the 30-day decline at $17.1 billion, marking the fastest contraction since June 2022.

Stablecoins provide much of the dollar liquidity used to purchase cryptocurrencies, so when investors redeem stablecoins for traditional dollars, the market loses potential buying power.

It has been revealed that bitcoin ETFs are sending another warning. US spot Bitcoin ETFs have lost $2.35 billion over two weeks, extending a difficult period for institutional demand. Corporate buying has weakened too. Public companies collectively sold 11,647 BTC worth approximately $869 million. Strategy remained a buyer, adding 1,037 BTC, but the wider corporate treasury trend has turned negative.

In a recent development, macroeconomic conditions are making the situation worse. Hotter-than-expected US inflation and employment figures have pushed interest-rate expectations higher. Futures markets now fully price a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December.

BREAKING: October PPI Inflation rises to 6.5%, its highest level since November 2022.Core PPI Inflation was 5.0%, in-line with expectations of 5.0%.CPI, PPI, and PCE inflation continue to push higher in the US.All signs point toward a December rate hike.

Higher rates strengthen the dollar and make non-yielding assets like Bitcoin less attractive. Meanwhile, the dollar index has climbed to 102.9, adding another headwind for crypto markets.

According to recent reports, coinbase Institutional also warned that Bitcoin could struggle to recover without renewed crypto-native demand. Its analysis places $62,000 among the notable support levels, with $58,000–$59,000 emerging as another potential downside target.

The technical picture remains fragile. Bitcoin needs to reclaim the $66,000–$68,000 region before bulls can establish a convincing recovery. A sustained move above $73,000–$75,000 would provide a much stronger reversal signal.

Industry observers note that bitcoin has already experienced a substantial correction, but the rebound hasn’t settled the argument. The bullish case rests on exhausted sellers, reduced speculative exposure, extreme fear, and buyers defending the $62,000 region. The bearish case rests on shrinking stablecoin supply, ETF withdrawals, weaker corporate accumulation, and rising borrowing costs.

Industry observers note that for now, liquidity remains the deciding factor. A genuine Bitcoin bottom needs more than liquidation-driven relief rallies. It needs fresh capital entering the market, institutional demand returning, and spot buyers absorbing available supply.

If stablecoin supply stabilizes and ETF flows turn positive, Bitcoin could build a foundation for its next recovery. But if capital continues leaving the ecosystem, the $62,000 floor could give way to another painful correction.

Bitcoin may be approaching its bottom, but the market hasn’t yet shown that buyers are ready to take control.

#18539. Reconciling the OCC’s Final Stablecoin Reserve Floors Against the Fed’s Proposal

Reconciling the OCC’s Final Stablecoin Reserve Floors Against the Fed’s Proposal

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1285 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The OCC's final GENIUS Act rule sets a 5% cash floor and a 40% cap on any one counterparty.
  • Issuers now face two sets of reserve rules that share a redemption deadline and differ on almost everything else.
  • Ask a stablecoin issuer what its reserves must look like in 2027, and the honest answer is now: it depends which regulator you ask.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

The OCC's final GENIUS Act rule sets a 5% cash floor and a 40% cap on any one counterparty. The Fed's open proposal uses neither figure, and its comment window runs until November 30.

Issuers now face two sets of reserve rules that share a redemption deadline and differ on almost everything else.

Ask a stablecoin issuer what its reserves must look like in 2027, and the honest answer is now: it depends which regulator you ask.

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) gave its answer on October 21, the final rule implementing the GENIUS Act. Our October 19 piece on staggered agency filings expected that rule "before the end of October," and it came two days later. The rule sets specific numbers: at least 5% of reserves in demand deposits or similar instant-access funds, and no more than 40% of reserves with a single counterparty.

Sources indicate that the Federal Reserve's answer is still a proposal. Its GENIUS Act rulemaking remains open for comment until November 30, and it contains neither of those numbers. Until the Fed finalizes its rule, any company planning to issue under both agencies' rules, or deciding which one to apply to, is working with one fixed set of numbers and one open-ended set of principles.

In a recent development, the OCC's final rule was published in the Federal Register on October 23 and takes effect on January 18, 2027, the same day as the GENIUS Act itself. Comptroller Jonathan V. Gould called it "a clear, practical framework for payment stablecoin innovation, with strong standards for reserve backing, redemption, and risk management.".

The reserve rules are looser than the March proposal in several places:.

Sources indicate that the OCC also removed the rebuttable presumption that some affiliate yield arrangements break the GENIUS Act's ban on paying interest, though it kept its broader anti-evasion powers. The agency received about 328 comments.

Sources indicate that for existing issuers, the timeline is short. Under OCC Bulletin 2026-51, firms already operating in the United States that file a "substantially complete" application by January 18 can generally expect a waiver of the prior-approval requirement.

It has been revealed that the Fed released its two proposals on September 24. They were published in the Federal Register on September 29 under Docket No. R-1899, and comments are due November 30.

Sources indicate that the main requirements proposal would require Board-supervised issuers to "fully back their stablecoins with certain permissible reserve assets". The reserves' fair value would have to equal or exceed the stablecoins' outstanding value at all times. Permissible assets include:.

It has been revealed that on diversification, however, the Fed sets no numbers. Reserves must be "sufficiently diverse" to keep one-to-one backing at all times, and issuers must manage concentration in uninsured deposits and repo counterparties. The Board claims it generally expects reserves to be mostly Treasuries, but it sets no cash floor and no counterparty percentage.

Sources indicate that redemption is where the two agencies agree most closely. Both define timely redemption as no later than two business days after a request. The difference lies in what happens under stress.

The FDIC, in its own proposal, uses a third approach: issuers would report on their own when redemption requests exceed 10% of issuance within 24 hours.

The clearest conflict is not about how much cash an issuer must hold, but how each agency treats bank deposits.

Under the OCC rule, at least 5% of reserves must be held in demand deposits or similar balances. That is a direct requirement to hold bank money.

Recent findings suggest that the Fed proposal has no deposit floor. Instead, it would charge 2% capital against reserves held as uninsured deposits at an insured bank, and the same charge applies to undercollateralized reverse repo. One agency requires a minimum amount in deposits, and the other makes issuers hold extra capital against the deposits they choose to keep.

Concentration works the same way. An issuer with 60% of its deposit reserves at one bank would breach the OCC's 40% cap, unless one of the custodian or government exemptions applies. Under the Fed's current text, that issuer would face only a judgment by its supervisor about whether it has managed concentration risk properly.

The rules for a reserve shortfall also differ:.

The difference is largest on capital. The OCC sets an individualized capital requirement measured in GAAP tangible equity. It has a $5 million floor that now lasts for the issuer's whole life, plus an operational backstop equal to 12 months of total expenses, up to half of which can be funded with qualifying subordinated debt.

In a recent development, the Fed proposes a fixed formula. On top of the 2% charges on deposits and repo, it adds an operational-risk charge on outstanding issuance:.

It also adds 25% of three-year average revenue from sources other than reserves, adjusted by a loss scalar.

For an issuer with $50 billion in circulation, the issuance charge alone works out to $850 million under the Fed's proposal, before the revenue add-on. The OCC rule has no comparable fixed figure. Its capital depends on the issuer's own risk profile, with the $5 million floor as the only set minimum.

Sources indicate that for now, the OCC's figures are final and the Fed's are not. Issuers and banks that hold reserves can still argue for changes until the Fed's comment period closes on November 30, and the Fed has asked 277 questions.

The decisions that matter most are clear from the comparison above:.

Both sets of rules apply from the same date, January 18, 2027. If the Fed's final rule keeps its current approach, the United States will begin regulating stablecoins with a common redemption deadline and two different reserve rulebooks, decided by which agency charters the issuer.

Latest Update: Inside the Properties James Bond Has Made Famous as Robert Pattinson Gears Up to Play 007

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1039 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s official: Robert Pattinson is stepping into the role of James Bond.
  • The news comes after years of speculation surrounding who might succeed Daniel Craig—who was the sixth actor to bring 007 to life, and portrayed the British spy in five films, ending with 2021’s “No Time To Die.”.
  • The official James Bond X account shared a first look of Pattinson donning the infamous tux for the role, captioned “Identity Confirmed.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s official: Robert Pattinson is stepping into the role of James Bond.

The news comes after years of speculation surrounding who might succeed Daniel Craig—who was the sixth actor to bring 007 to life, and portrayed the British spy in five films, ending with 2021’s “No Time To Die.”.

The official James Bond X account shared a first look of Pattinson donning the infamous tux for the role, captioned “Identity Confirmed.”.

Recent findings suggest that “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” Pattinson noted in a statement. “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement.”.

Director Denis Villeneuve alluded to the search for the next Bond in the statement.

Recent findings suggest that “I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey,” the “Dune” director remarked. “We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007.”.

Dozens of potential candidates have been floated as possibilities since Craig’s reign came to an end, including Idris Elba, Jacob Elordi, Callum Turner, and John Hardy.

Bond first walked onto the silver screen in 1962, when Sean Connery brought the iconic book character to life in the first film, “Dr. No.” There have been a whopping 25 Bond films so far, with Pattinson suiting up for the 26th.

After seven films, Connery ended his run in 1983 with “Never Say Never.” In 1969, George Lazenby became the only actor to star in a single film in the franchise, with “On Her Majesty’s Secret Service.”.

Roger Moore held the role from 1973 to 1985, also impressively holding the gig for seven titles. Next up was Timothy Dalton, who starred in two films between 1987 and 1989.

Pierce Brosnan reinvigorated the franchise when he became Bond in 1995, holding the job until 2002. In 2006, Craig ushered in a new era, tackling 007 with a more rough-and-tumble edge.

Perhaps even more impressive than the scale of actors who have taken their martinis shaken, not stirred, is the sheer number of filming locations the franchise has made its mark on for over 60 years.

Hunting Bond, a fan site that tracks the locations, has identified nearly 600 filming spots across the world. While the James Bond universe is certainly action-packed, it’s also quite aspirational, and has often provided viewers with rich backgrounds and fascinating properties that became characters in their own right.

It would be nearly impossible to rank all of the lavish homes Bond has stepped foot in over the years, but there are definitely a handful that stand out in memory.

Even without a connection to one of the Bond films with the strongest pop culture staying power—”Diamonds Are Forever,” of course—the Elrod House in Palm Springs, CA, is an incredible dwelling.

Perched on a hillside overlooking Coachella Valley, the 8,900-square-foot home was designed by modernist architect John Lautner for interior designer Arthur Elrod.

The fascinating structure has a concrete dome-shaped roof, a circular living room, and a half-moon swimming pool that Connery’s Bond threw an enemy into during a heated fight scene.

Villa Sylva is a picturesque Greek estate that’s appeared in a handful of movies, including Moore’s “For Your Eyes Only”—although in the film, it assumed the role of the Madrid home of hitman Hector Gonzales.

The 12-bedroom luxury villa boasts unobstructed views of the Ionian Sea and is perched on an idyllic 10-acre property. Today, it can be rented as a wedding venue or a vacation home sleeping up to 18 people.

It has been revealed that given Bond’s vital role at the UK-based M16, it only makes sense that at least some of the locations had to be local. The sprawling Luton Hoo Estate was a location in Brosnan’s 1999 film, “The World Is Not Enough” and Connery’s 1983 return for “Never Say Never Again.”.

It’s also been featured in dozens of other projects, including “Downton Abbey.”.

Built in 1903, the property is about an hour’s drive from London—a journey that would probably be cut in half when Bond is behind the wheel. The historic English country estate spans more than 1,000 acres and has a handful of structures—most notably, a five-star hotel and an exquisite mansion.

Craig’s Bond debut in the 2006 film, “Casino Royale,” was set in the breathtaking Ocean Club in the Bahamas.

The luxury resort has a number of sea-view villas for rent, including one that served as the perfect backdrop for a romantic scene between the spy and Solange Dimitrios, the wife of villain Alex Dimitrios.

Sources indicate that although Bond was just a visitor, the Ocean Club does have “67 turnkey oceanfront residences” available for ownership. The ultraprivate oceanfront abodes are available in a variety of sizes between two- and five-bedroom. Pricing begins at $7.5 million, according to the Ocean Club’s website.

It’s never been captured on screen in a Bond film, but 007 creator Ian Fleming built a bungalow called GoldenEye in Port Antonio, Jamaica.

The private estate is where the prolific author wrote all 13 of the original James Bond novels. Eventually, it was sold and turned into a resort, which is still called GoldenEye today. The property has been vastly expanded in the decades since Fleming, who died in 1964, lived there. It now includes lagoon cottages, villas, beach huts, and a spa.

The 25th Bond film, “No Time To Die,” provided a nod to the character’s birthplace. According to Architectural Digest, there’s a replica of Fleming’s desk in the opening scene of the film. Like the writer, Bond lives in a Jamaican bungalow in this installation, but it was built from scratch solely for filming.

Goodbye, manual work: AI-native CRM platform Dreamteam raises $53M to automate enterprise sales

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1435 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Intelligent sales software startup Dreamteam AI Inc.
  • The funds come by way of a seed and Series A round led by Accel Partners with participation from Together Fund and Premji Invest.
  • CRM platforms such as Salesforce and Hubspot have served as vital cogs in the wheel sales-focused enterprises for more than a quarter of a century.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 16 2026.

Intelligent sales software startup Dreamteam AI Inc. said today it has raised $53 million in early-stage funding to try to flip the narrative around customer relationship management platforms, which often seem like more of a hindrance than a help, by actually getting work done for sales teams.

The funds come by way of a seed and Series A round led by Accel Partners with participation from Together Fund and Premji Invest.

CRM platforms such as Salesforce and Hubspot have served as vital cogs in the wheel sales-focused enterprises for more than a quarter of a century. But these days they often create just as much work as they save, claims Dreamteam co-founder and Chief Executive Anand Venkatraman (pictured, center, alongside co-founders Ramesh Parthasarathy and Senthil Kanthaswamy). While organizations are striving to use artificial intelligence to automate more of their business processes, CRMs are holding them back, he believes.

According to recent reports, the problem with legacy CRM platforms is that they’re totally reliant on manual data entry, Venkatraman explained. Because their architectures are built around structured data fields and rigid, hand-coded workflows, they create a tight bottleneck that makes it almost impossible for autonomous AI agents that feed primarily on semantic data to get anything done.

“When a sales prospect expresses price hesitation or mentions a competitor, a salesperson registers it immediately,” he said. “But a legacy CRM, starving for unstructured nuance, misses it entirely, leaving AI agents without the vital context needed to reason effectively.”.

It has been revealed that to provide this context, Dreamteam has rebuilt the CRM from the ground up around the idea of a “firm brain,” or a living memory of the business that constantly updates itself by ingesting new information from meetings with clients, prospects and team members, emails and other connected tools. As with all AI-native platforms, there’s also a generous dose of automation in the shape of four AI agents, or teammates, which specialize in different tasks.

The agents include Rachel, which handles account research; Sally for meeting preparations and follow-ups; Raj, which monitors for pipeline risks; and Alex, which serves as the CRM administrator, keeping the platform ticking over without any human intervention.

Sources indicate that venkatraman said he and his co-founders designed Dreamteam’s architecture specifically to address the historic shortcomings of legacy CRM platforms, which struggle to dig up the most vital business intelligence, leaving teams flying blind. “When a CEO asks why the quarter’s three biggest deals were lost, RevOps spends two weeks building a partial answer from whatever the reps happened to type,” he said. “The richest signals from meetings, emails, and calls were never captured, so the answer is always incomplete and always late.”.

Legacy CRMs also fail to capture institutional knowledge, which means that everything a senior sales representative knows about the clients they work with leaves when they depart the organization. There’s also a heavy administrative tax, with owners forced to waste valuable time entering data to keep the platform up to date.

“CRMs don’t have a shortage of features,” Venkatraman mentioned. “But they have a shortage of context and trust, and they lack the ability to get actual work done.”.

Dreamteam does things differently. By capturing the unspoken context around each deal an organization does, it says, its platform can help to prevent latest leads from going stale. Monitoring everything that’s said and agreed to in meetings, via chats and emails and other tools, the platform can pick out the most important signals, such as pricing sensitivities, objections and stakeholder dynamics.

It remembers all of the fine details of each specific deal. That way, even if the main sales rep involved suddenly leaves, it will retain all of the context so whoever takes over the account knows what needs to be done next.

The platform also employs humanlike reasoning. “When a prospect states, ‘The board is pushing hard on costs,’ it knows the proposal should lead with ROI, not features,” Venkatraman explained. “The CRM was supposed to give companies a complete picture of their customers, yet the richest parts of that picture have always lived outside the CRM.”.

Industry observers note that the startup has already witnessed significant traction with its agentic, contextual approach: It’s used by hundreds of organizations across the AI, healthcare, manufacturing, consulting and online media sectors. Dreamteam has enabled those early adopters to transform the way they handle sales.

Sources indicate that because the CRM continuously self-updates its records following daily customer interactions, it means sales people have much more time to focus on actually selling rather than data entry. Senior leaders have more visibility into deal pipelines, and can immediately find out why deals are stalling or how their customer’s sentiments are shifting.

Sources indicate that scott Olechowski, chief product officer at the video streaming service Plex Inc., mentioned he was especially taken with the tight level of integration with Dreamteam and the company’s existing information technology stack. “The combination of simplicity and power hits the sweet spot for us,” he said. “The ability to integrate with the AI tools we are using across our organization is a game-changer.”.

Industry observers note that venkatraman believes Dreamteam can have an even greater impact in future by expanding its shared intelligence layer beyond sales operations. His ambition is to build a platform that spans the entire customer lifecycle, from onboarding to customer success, renewals and upselling, to ensure that organizations can squeeze the most value out of the deal context it captures.

“Much of what’s learned during sales is lost or fragmented when a customer moves into implementation or customer success,” he pointed out. “But the same firm brain that knows why a customer bought should also help teams onboard them, spot risks and find ways to grow the relationship.”.

Industry observers note that one way Dreamteam intends to pursue this vision is through what it calls “Magic Apps,” which is a capability that lets people build custom dashboards and tailored CRM workflows using natural language prompts. “The apps live inside Dreamteam, inherit its data permissions and action-level authorizations, and stay connected to customer records, workflows and the Tech giant Brain, so you can customize without rebuilding the foundation,” Venkatraman said.

Premji Invest’s Saravanan Nattanmai has already bought into this vision, stressing the need for CRM systems to become more than just a system of record. He characterizes what Dreamteam is building as a “system of intelligence.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Dreamteam sets out to intuitively understand user intent, build deep contextual intelligence and execute workflows seamlessly through autonomous AI teammates,” he said. “We believe the future of enterprise software lies in AI-native systems that don’t just augment existing workflows but fundamentally reimagine how work gets done.”.

#18535. Latest Update: October Marks the First Month in 3 Years With a Decline in U.S. Home-Sale Prices

Latest Update: October Marks the First Month in 3 Years With a Decline in U.S. Home-Sale Prices

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1033 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Redfin

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • home-sale prices rose from a year earlier every single month, even as mortgage rates climbed and would-be buyers pulled back.
  • It has been revealed that the median home-sale price declined 0.4% year over year to $388,634 in October.
  • With the total number of homes for sale at its highest level since early 2020 and demand cooling, homebuyers’ negotiating power keeps increasing–and that’s finally showing up in sale prices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For three years, U.S. home-sale prices rose from a year earlier every single month, even as mortgage rates climbed and would-be buyers pulled back. That streak has ended.

It has been revealed that the median home-sale price declined 0.4% year over year to $388,634 in October. That’s  the first decline since May 2023 and a sharp slowdown from the 2.5% gain just two months earlier. With Americans’ wages growing about 4% year over year, even a slight dip in prices can improve affordability. Sale prices have risen nearly every single month for the last 13 years; the only exception was a handful of months in 2023.

With the total number of homes for sale at its highest level since early 2020 and demand cooling, homebuyers’ negotiating power keeps increasing–and that’s finally showing up in sale prices.

Recent findings suggest that home-sale prices fell nationwide, but they rose in more than half of the 50 most populous U.S. metro areas. San Francisco led the nation by a wide margin, with the median sale price rising 16.8% year over year. That’s the biggest increase since 2018. Next comes New Brunswick, NJ, with a 7.7% gain. Two other NYC-area metros also had price increases ranking in the top six; the median sale price rose 4.4% in both New York City and Nassau County.

Recent findings suggest that in San Francisco, AI wealth is fueling competition for scarce inventory; active listings were down 7% from a year earlier. In the Upcoming York City area, years of limited homebuilding have left buyers competing for relatively few homes in a region with a strong job market.

Home-sale prices fell most in Austin, TX, where they declined 6.5% year over year. It’s followed by Seattle (-5.1%) and Nashville, TN (-4.9%). Austin and Nashville are among the biggest buyer’s markets in the U.S., and Seattle’s shaky tech job market is curbing demand.

National sale prices are losing steam because fewer Americans can afford to buy a home. U.S. pending home sales fell 3.6% from a month earlier in October on a seasonally adjusted basis to their lowest level since 2013, with the exception of April 2020.

This is a real-time indicator of the state of the housing market; fewer homes went under contract in October largely because mortgage rates averaged 7.33%, a three-year high and up from 6.86% the month before.

All figures in this report are seasonally adjusted, with the exception of median sale price data and mortgage rate data. See a more detailed methodology here and view an interactive dashboard here.

“It’s a buyer’s market, but not many people can afford to buy,” stated Chen Zhao, Redfin’s head of economics. “That could start to shift a bit, now that sale prices are closer to reflecting the shape of the market. House hunters in most of the country should know that the price they see on a listing may very well be a starting point; they should try offering below the asking price, and negotiating for closing costs, repairs and maybe even mortgage-rate buydowns. If you can’t get the price or monthly payment you want on one house, move on to the next one–with a big pool of inventory sitting on the market, buyers can afford to be picky.”.

It has been revealed that pending home sales declined in all of the most populous U.S. metros. That’s the second month in a row that has happened; before September, the last time was three years earlier.

Recent findings suggest that the biggest declines were in Seattle and San Diego, both places where pending sales fell more than 20% year over year. Those West Coast metros are some of the priciest in the U.S., so 7%-plus mortgages hit house hunters’ monthly payments there hard. In Seattle, an uncertain local job market is also curbing demand.

Closed home sales fell to their lowest level in nearly 3 years. They declined 2.1% month over month in October to their lowest level since December 2023; before that, the last time sales dropped that low was 2014. Many of the deals that closed last month went under contract in August and September, when rates were already climbing and economic uncertainty was deterring a lot of house hunters.

According to recent reports, with homebuying demand falling, supply is building. The total number of homes for sale rose 0.9% from September to its highest level since early 2020; that’s the biggest monthly gain since May 2025.

More supply gives buyers more homes to choose from and more leverage:.

In a recent development, “Buyers are nervous about rates, the economy, and everything they’re seeing in the news– so they need the house and the price to line up perfectly before they’ll make an offer,” said Callie Kimmel, a Redfin Premier agent in Philadelphia. “I’m advising sellers to price just below current market value from day one–and not comps from six months ago, but homes that are listed right now. Otherwise, the home is likely to end up sitting on the market for a bit and selling for less than they hoped. There are a few exceptions: Move-in ready homes in the most desirable neighborhoods are still competitive; in those cases, sellers have the upper hand.”.

While total housing supply is growing, fewer sellers are adding new inventory to the pool. New listings of homes for sale fell 1% month over month to the lowest level in more than two years. Would-be sellers are pulling back as homebuying demand slows and sale prices lose steam.

Aging Parents and Empty Nests Force Homeowners To Rethink Layouts Years Before the Move

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most homeowners know their homes may need updates to accommodate their changing needs as they age.
  • Instead of waiting until those changes are necessary, they’re investing in renovations years in advance to prepare for aging parents who might eventually move in after their children leave the nest.
  • It has been revealed that angi’s 2026 State of Home Spending Pulse study found that 66% of homeowners blueprint to make a major home investment within the next five years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most homeowners know their homes may need updates to accommodate their changing needs as they age.

Some, however, are thinking even further ahead.

Instead of waiting until those changes are necessary, they’re investing in renovations years in advance to prepare for aging parents who might eventually move in after their children leave the nest.

It has been revealed that angi’s 2026 State of Home Spending Pulse study found that 66% of homeowners blueprint to make a major home investment within the next five years. And the 2027 Home Trends To Watch report predicts that 2027 will be the year they take a proactive approach and focus on creating a home that grows with them.

If you own your home, experts agree that you should anticipate how your needs could change in the next five to 10 years and use that information to guide your long-term home improvement goals today.

By doing so, you can make the most out of your renovation budget, avoid costly last-minute adjustments, and ensure your home comfortably adapts to the different stages of life.

Matt Plaskoff, CEO and founder of One Week Bath in Los Angeles, is seeing this proactive, multigenerational "future-proofing” trend among his clients.

“It comes down to people having heard stories of it going the other way. Mom falls or receives a diagnosis, and suddenly the family is trying to put in a walk-in shower and grab bars on short notice while suddenly incurring more costs with doctors and insurance,” states Plaskoff.

Recent findings suggest that multigenerational living is also at an all-time high, and the recent National Association of Realtors® Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers report reflects this shift. It found that 17% of homes purchased last year were intended for multigenerational households.

And when adult kids leave, there’s suddenly more space that makes it easier to create a home that works well for both aging in place and aging parents.

We can’t forget the housing affordability crisis forcing families to rethink the homes they already own.

“The house may no longer fit the household, but buying a better-fitting home can mean a higher price, a higher mortgage rate, and higher monthly expenses,” notes Jon Brooks, co-founder of Momentum Realty in Jacksonville, FL.

Plus, it's more cost-effective to future-proof your home when you blueprint properly and actually have the funds to support your projects.

According to recent reports, “The worst time to remodel is when you don’t have the budget for it. You make decisions that should take time and careful planning under pressure and may just accept whatever contractor can show up ASAP, even if it means you have to pay more,” states Plaskoff.

There is also a practical side.

If you're already opening up walls for a bath remodel, for example, adding blocking for future grab bars, widening a doorway, or adding a curbless shower will be faster and cheaper than if you were to come back later and redo finished work.

Experts agree that a strong universal design features a functional yet beautiful bathroom with a wider doorway, good lighting, lever handles for knobs, a walk-in shower, and slip-resistant flooring.

“If done right, it feels more like a spa than a hospital, and that’s what matters most to those who are using it every day,” Plaskoff explains.

A home that supports privacy and independence is just as important.

“An example can be a primary suite on the ground floor with its own bathroom, or a room with a separate entrance. Parents want to keep their routines and privacy, without having to sacrifice accessibility,” claims Plaskoff.

You might also consider adding a second structure to your backyard like an accessory dwelling unit or tiny home.

“For families with the space, an ADU is one of the best solutions we see. It gives an aging parent true independence, with their own kitchen, bath, and front door, while keeping them close enough for daily connection and support,” explains Michelle Squire, designer and principal at Studio SQUARE in San Francisco.

If long-term resale is important to you, be sure to consider what buyers value in your neighborhood. This way you can determine where to make permanent changes and where to keep things flexible.

“If you’re overimproving for the area, just understand you may have a harder time recouping that money if you choose to sell,” says Christina Rordam, real estate agent at Florida Realty Investments in Orlando, FL.

At the end of the day, prioritize flexibility, try not to over improve for the neighborhood you’re in, and most importantly, consider what works best for you and your family.

Engel & Völkers confirmed an Aruba shop, Realty of America entered San Diego, and eXp Realty added a Tampa Bay brokerage and an Ohio team.

In a recent development, brokerage expansion stretched from the Caribbean to the West Coast in recent days, as firms moved into new markets and picked up agents and teams from other companies. Engel & Völkers is headed to Aruba, where it aims to open a shop in April 2027, and Realty of America reached California with Zandra Ulloa and 12 of her Team Z Realty agents in San Diego.

eXp Realty picked up a Tampa Bay brokerage and a Cincinnati-area team that spent 20 years with REMAX. Baird & Warner brought on Oak Park, Illinois, boutique Beyond Properties, and Dane Briggs teamed up with Phil Sexton at HomeSmart’s NEXT team. IRES MLS welcomed back a former staffer to run operations, and Howard Hanna Portside added an agent in Massachusetts.

Recent findings suggest that engel & Völkers expanded into Aruba with license partners Zobaida Akkari and Richard Franken, Aruba-based entrepreneurs with backgrounds in real estate, luxury sales, hospitality and tourism. The shop is projected to open in April 2027 at L.G. Smith Blvd. 330 in Palm Beach and will serve clients across the island, according to the tech giant.

“Aruba is a compelling addition to the network’s growing presence in the Caribbean,” Stuart Siegel, president and CEO of Engel & Völkers Americas, noted in a statement.

Realty of America entered California with Zandra Ulloa and 12 Team Z Realty agent partners in San Diego. Ulloa has generated more than $4.2 billion in sales volume over her 13-year career, and Team Z peaked at 72 agents and $589 million in annual volume, according to the tech giant. Agent-owned ROA, founded in September 2024, states it has more than 3,900 agents across 26 markets.

“People around me may see what I am giving up, but I see what I am making room for,” Ulloa remarked in a statement.

Rene Carpena and Dana Carpena moved Florida’s 1st Choice Realty, their independent Greater Tampa Bay brokerage, to eXp Realty, where it now operates as 1st Choice Collective. The group brings more than 70 agents and support staff and recorded more than 325 transactions and $60 million in sales volume in 2025, according to the company.

Industry observers note that jon Bowling also brought his 17-person team in Mason, Ohio, to eXp after 20 years with RE/MAX. eXp Realty is the core subsidiary of AGNT Inc.

According to recent reports, baird & Warner added Beyond Properties, a boutique brokerage in Oak Park, Illinois, whose dozen agents will operate as Beyond Properties Group. Owner and designated managing broker Erica Cuneen, who founded the firm almost 20 years ago, will co-lead the group with team leader Cynthia Howe Gajewski. The group joins Baird & Warner’s Oak Park office and keeps its Marion Street location.

“This partnership will allow me to simplify the operational side of the business and spend more time doing what I love, which is focusing on our agents and clients,” Cuneen said in a statement.

According to recent reports, dane Briggs, an Arizona real estate veteran, partnered with Phil Sexton, founder of HomeSmart’s NEXT team, in a leadership role focused on agent workflows and AI integrations. Briggs has worked as a designated broker and title executive, founded referral brokerage Roosted and led expansion initiatives at Homie. He has also served as an Inman Ambassador.

“Before long, we weren’t just talking about what Phil was building. We were talking about what we could build together,” Briggs noted in a statement.

It has been revealed that IRES MLS, which serves Northern Colorado and parts of the Front Range, rehired Samantha Ewing as director of operations. Ewing spent 13 years at IRES as a projects manager and quality assurance tester before leaving in 2018, and she has more than 20 years of experience in MLS operations and real estate technology.

“Having Samantha return to IRES is an exciting opportunity for our team and the local industry we serve,” CEO Julie Dahl stated in a statement.

Industry observers note that howard Hanna Portside Real Estate Group added Melissa Winter, an agent with nearly 15 years of experience who focuses on first-time homebuyers, to its Massachusetts team in Amesbury. Portside, which has more than 200 agents, entered a strategic partnership with Howard Hanna in 2026, according to the manufacturer.

“What drew me to Portside was the energy, the people, and the opportunity for growth,” Winter said in a statement.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Called exploit_agent, the framework turned up on an exposed staging server, where it was wired into several frontier and locally hosted large language models.
  • Data taken from victims was sitting on the same server, alongside scripts for brute-forcing, installing webshells and even removing webshells left by rival attackers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 16 2026.

A fresh report out today from Google LLC’s Google Threat Intelligence Group finds that for the first time, attackers have used an artificial intelligence framework running with no human in the loop to turn security patches into exploits.

Called exploit_agent, the framework turned up on an exposed staging server, where it was wired into several frontier and locally hosted large language models. Its job, according to GTIG, is continuous comparison of popular web application code before and after each patch announcement. Once a likely flaw is identified, the exploit it drafts is executed automatically.

Data taken from victims was sitting on the same server, alongside scripts for brute-forcing, installing webshells and even removing webshells left by rival attackers. Victim telemetry suggests the operator was most interested in French websites tied to media, entertainment and education. Written in Russian, one comment in the framework’s configuration file tells whoever set it up to enter the keys “right here, not in the chat.”.

In the previous edition of the quarterly tracker two months ago, GTIG mentioned it had not observed fully autonomous attack pipelines deployed against targets in the wild. That changed over the past quarter, according to the latest report, titled “Agentic Threat Activity Crosses a Significant Threshold.” Because the source material for a patched flaw is finite, GTIG believes attackers may find it more efficient to point LLMs at n-day vulnerabilities than to hunt for zero-days.

How quickly the gap between disclosure and a working exploit can close reveals in the case of two flaws in print management servers from PaperCut Software Pty Ltd., chained together and exploited as zero-days in late August. Security researchers and Huntress Labs Inc. used large language models to generate working exploits within a day of disclosure.

A campaign tracked by GreyNoise Intelligence Inc. four days after disclosure is believed to have relied on LLMs to build its exploits before it hit hundreds of organizations. One foothold in that campaign reached domain administrator within minutes, GreyNoise found.

Industry observers note that elsewhere, open-source agentic penetration testing frameworks are being used to automate discrete steps of live intrusions. During one intrusion against the U.S. aerospace sector, a threat actor was observed using the multi-agent framework CAIRN.

Another actor ran a customized platform built on PentAGI between late August and early October to scan a wide range of organizations in Asia for vulnerabilities. For now, the noisy forensic trail left by unrestricted autonomous execution is said to make the frameworks easier to detect.

According to recent reports, according to GTIG, influence operations now use models for far more than writing posts. Using cloud phone farms, a turnkey platform that one commercial contractor was building with help from the Gemini API is designed to run more than 100,000 social media accounts. To make generated photos pass as smartphone shots, prompts behind a separate platform, which targeted political sentiment across Europe and the Middle East, are stated to have called for deliberate camera flaws.

Recent findings suggest that among government-backed actors, photos on the fake recruiter profiles that a suspected North Korean group tracked as UNC6836 used to approach cryptocurrency organizations in North America and Europe were found to carry Google’s SynthID watermarks. By way of altered .claude/settings.json files in internal code repositories, the group later rigged each launch of Anthropic PBC’s Claude Code to download its SOMBERMEME backdoor.

Recent findings suggest that google noted it disabled the accounts and assets tied to the Gemini misuse it found. Google DeepMind has also used the findings to strengthen its classifiers.

Mauricio: I don’t know. We’ll just keep going. I really like that show Traitors. I would love to be on that show. That could be a fun one for me, so I’m putting that out into the universe.

Alexia: My dream would be to do a reality TV show with my family … We did Buying Beverly Hills, and we’ve done Real Housewives for like [16] years now. But we’ve never done something all of us together, just us, and I think that’ll be really cool.

It has been revealed that mauricio: I’m going to leave that one on the table. If anything, it’s for 2030. There’s still plenty of time to do that and make that decision. But I love LA, and I think I can help LA a lot. I think we live in an amazing city, and if the moment comes, and I’m set up in the right position in the business and I feel like I can actually win, I might do it. But I wouldn’t do it if I didn’t feel like I could actually win.

Mauricio: It’s an absolute mess, what’s going on in our in our in our industry right now, particularly with the listings. My take is, it’s quite simple. I think that there’s a lot of change that’s happening. I believe that it’s somewhere in the middle. Like I do everything.

I believe sellers should have choice, but I believe that we should be sharing those private listings amongst everybody — every agent, every brokerage firm, not just keeping it for themselves. I feel like there’s a lot happening right now in the industry where everybody’s really looking out for themselves: the MLSs, NAR, Compass.

Actually, Compass, I think, wants to collaborate, wants to share, but they’re in a massive, big fight. But in the meantime, this Clear Cooperation Policy is what is allowing them to keep all the listings to themselves and not share them … The PLS is exactly what that was, and I still think that if Clear Cooperation Policy didn’t pass, it would have been an amazing business to have right now.

Mauricio: We are really positioned as the premier luxury brokerage firm outside of Compass right now. They’ve got Sotheby’s, they’ve got Christie’s, they’ve got all of those different brands, and we’re the only independent luxury brokerage firm out there right now.

Industry observers note that so I’m excited to be in that position. Competitors make you better every single day … I’m excited in terms of where we sit, where we stand in a very difficult time; I’m not excited about the market. We really need to do some things to improve it. We’ve had three years of very, very difficult conditions, and it’s going to be very difficult for people to survive. And those that do survive will come out better.

In a recent development, I think we’re in a good position to survive, but we’ve got our work cut out for us over the next year, year and a half. But we’ll continue to grow. We’ll continue to expand, and I’m excited to just be a part of this industry. But man, it’s hard out there right now.

#18529. Tech Report: Just 3 Major U.S. Metros Are Seller’s Markets–the Fewest Since the Pandemic Freeze

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1347 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Redfin ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Just 3 Major U.S. Metros Are Seller’s Markets–the Fewest Since the Pandemic Freeze

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1347 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Redfin

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, just three of the 50 most populous U.S.
  • Sources indicate that nassau County, NY was the number-one seller’s market, with 24.7% fewer sellers than buyers.
  • In a recent development, all three seller’s markets became less strong seller’s markets in October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, just three of the 50 most populous U.S. metro areas were seller’s markets in October. That’s tied for the fewest in records dating back to 2016, matching April 2020, when the pandemic froze the housing market.

Sources indicate that nassau County, NY was the number-one seller’s market, with 24.7% fewer sellers than buyers. The other seller’s markets were Newark, NJ (-14.3%) and Montgomery County, PA (-12.1%).

In a recent development, all three seller’s markets became less strong seller’s markets in October. In Nassau County, there were 28.3% fewer sellers than buyers in September, a bigger gap than October’s 24.7%. Newark’s gap shrunk from 17.6% to 14.3%, and Montgomery County’s shrunk from 20.1% to 12.1%. Milwaukee, which was a seller’s market in September, is now balanced, meaning it doesn’t favor sellers or buyers.

Sources indicate that the seller’s markets are places where limited homebuilding has kept housing supply tight. In the greater Fresh York City area, combine that with strong demand for homes near a major job center, and buyers are competing for homes. Home-sale prices rose an average of 3.3% year over year across the three seller’s markets in October. That’s compared with a 0.3% uptick across all of the buyer’s markets, a sign that in seller’s markets, competition among buyers is pushing up home prices.

In a recent development, “Buyers looking in these pockets of the Northeast should be prepared for a very different experience than buyers elsewhere in the country,” mentioned Redfin Senior Economist Asad Khan. “They may have less room to negotiate, especially on desirable, move-in-ready homes, and could face multiple-offer situations. If you’re shopping in one of these markets, it’s especially notable to know your budget, be ready to act when the right home comes along and avoid getting swept up in a bidding war.”.

Seller’s markets are the exception to a national picture that heavily favors buyers.

Industry observers note that nationwide, homebuyers have more negotiating power than at any point in Redfin’s records. There were an estimated 70.5% more home sellers than buyers in the U.S. housing market in October, the biggest gap in records dating back to 2013.

That marks the sixth record-breaking month in a row, and the margin is up from 65.6% in September. The Sun Belt is driving the extreme buyer’s market nationwide, led by huge seller surpluses in Miami, Nashville, TN and Las Vegas.

Recent findings suggest that when sellers outnumber buyers, buyers typically have more negotiating power because they have options. That’s why a market with a lot more sellers than buyers is considered a buyer’s market. We define a market where there are over 10% more sellers than buyers as a buyer’s market and a market where there are over 10% fewer sellers than buyers as a seller’s market. A market where the gap is plus or minus 10% is considered a balanced market.

We estimated the number of buyers using proprietary Redfin data on the typical time from a buyer’s first tour to close of purchase, and MLS data on active listings and pending sales. The estimated number of sellers in the market is simply the number of active listings in the MLS. These estimates are seasonally adjusted and subject to revision. See a more detailed methodology here and view an interactive dashboard here.

In a recent development, it’s only a buyer’s market for people who can afford to buy. High housing costs and economic jitters have pushed many would-be homebuyers to back off in recent years, creating the imbalance between buyers and sellers we see today.

Recent findings suggest that “A buyer-friendly market can help make homeownership a little more attainable, even if it doesn’t solve the affordability challenges that have kept many people on the sidelines,” Khan stated. “Sellers are increasingly competing for buyers’ attention, which can translate into price reductions, concessions and other savings. First-time buyers don’t have equity from a previous home to put toward a purchase, which makes saving for a down payment a big hurdle–but they also don’t have to sell a home before they can buy or give up a low mortgage rate. With a historic buyer’s market and home prices that are finally ticking down after three years of increases, first-time buyers who have been waiting–and can afford today’s costs–may have an opportunity to make a move.”.

The gap between buyers and sellers widened in October because would-be buyers retreated, while sellers continued listing their homes, albeit at a sluggish pace.

There were an estimated 895,752 homebuyers in the market nationwide in October, the lowest level in records dating back to 2013. That’s down 2% from a month earlier, the sixth straight monthly decline. Mortgage rates averaged 7.33% in October, up from 6.86% in September, which priced out more would-be buyers.

On the flip side, there were an estimated 1,526,984 home sellers in the market, the most since March 2020. That’s up 0.9% month over month.

Industry observers note that the number of homes on the market is piling up because many homes are lingering on the market for months without going under contract. Each month, more new listings are adding to the major pool of supply.

In a recent development, some homeowners keep listing their houses despite falling demand because many have given up on waiting for lower rates. They may want to sell now because they’re worried prices could decline, and some need to move for a new job, a growing family, or another life change. But many homeowners who don’t need to move have substantial equity and little pressure to sell, so they may hold off on listing.

Sources indicate that over 80% of U.S. metro areas, 41 of the 50 Redfin analyzed, are buyer’s markets. That matches September’s record.

For the third month in a row, Miami and Nashville have the biggest surpluses of sellers over buyers. Miami had 195.8% more sellers than buyers in October, and Nashville had 159.5% more. Las Vegas (149.9%) was third on the list. In the top 13 buyer’s markets, there were more than twice as many sellers as buyers in October. Nearly all are in the Sun Belt; four are in Texas and four are in Florida.

The Sun Belt, particularly Texas and Florida, is home to some of the nation’s biggest buyer’s markets, partly because of robust homebuilding. Builders are continuing to add new homes even as demand cools, swelling inventory and giving buyers more options and negotiating power.

According to recent reports, demand has cooled largely because rising mortgage rates and stubbornly high home prices are pricing buyers out. In Florida, rising HOA and homeowners insurance costs are exacerbating the affordability squeeze.

Six metros were “balanced” in October, neither buyer’s nor seller’s markets: Chicago (8.1% more sellers than buyers), Boston (7.5%), Providence, RI (7.5%), Newly introduced Brunswick, NJ (5.6%), Milwaukee (0.6% fewer sellers than buyers) and San Francisco (6.9% fewer).

The surplus of home sellers over buyers grew month over month in 34 of the 41 buyer’s markets in October.

The surplus increased most in Miami, which also has the biggest surplus of sellers over buyers; there were 195.8% more sellers than buyers in October, up from 160.5% the month before. The next-biggest monthly increases were in Las Vegas, where there were 149.9% more sellers than buyers, up from 122.8%, and Nashville (159.5%, up from 134.3%).

In a recent development, house hunters lost negotiating power in seven buyer’s markets. The surplus of sellers over buyers fell from September to October in Fort Worth, TX (91.6%, down from 100%), St. Louis (23.1%, down from 27.1%), Austin (124.8%, down from 128.2%), Dallas (118.6%, down from 120.5%), Jacksonville, FL, Pittsburgh and Los Angeles. All of them remain buyer’s markets.

Recent findings suggest that as a data journalist at Redfin, Dana Anderson writes about the numbers behind real estate trends.
